new_environment.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: default name given to an environment created with “+ Add” on the Environments tab, until the user types a real name.

new_project.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: default name given to a project created with “+ Add” on the Projects tab, until the user types a real name.

pick_color_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: button beside the color input and swatch that opens an inline color picker below it; changes to “Close Picker” while open.

project_singular.location: Connection Management → Projects pane → Editor: heading of the first group, holding the Name field, when a project is selected; singular noun.

projects_tab.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Tabs: second tab along the top, listing the projects that connections can be grouped under.

query_protections_section.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form: section heading above the safety checkboxes (read-only, confirmations, Touch ID, rollback) applied to every connection in this client, project or environment.

remove_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: button beside “+ Add” that deletes the selected client, project or environment; disabled when nothing is selected.

removed.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after Remove deletes the selected client, project or environment.

safety_ai_review_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require AI review for data changes” checkbox; data-changing statements must get an AI-written review before they run.
safety_ai_review_description.value: Requerir una revisión generada por IA antes de ejecutar instrucciones que modifiquen datos.

safety_ai_review_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that requires an AI review before INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and similar statements run.
safety_ai_review_label.value: Requerir revisión de IA para los cambios de datos

safety_confirmation_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the confirmation-dialog checkbox; the user is asked to confirm before any data-changing statement runs.
safety_confirmation_description.value: Pedir confirmación antes de ejecutar instrucciones que modifiquen datos.

safety_confirmation_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that shows a confirmation dialog before data-changing statements are run.
safety_confirmation_label.value: Requerir un diálogo de confirmación antes de ejecutar

safety_production_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Production environment” checkbox; connections stay read-only until writes are unlocked for a limited time, and each change asks for confirmation with its SQL.
safety_production_description.value: Las conexiones de este entorno son de solo lectura hasta que desbloquees las escrituras durante un período limitado, y cada cambio de datos pedirá confirmación mostrando el SQL exacto.

safety_production_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: first checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that marks the entry as production, turning on read-only mode and timed write unlocks.

safety_rollback_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the transaction + rollback checkbox; each executed batch runs inside a transaction that is always rolled back, so no changes persist.
safety_rollback_description.value: Ejecutar cada lote en una transacción que se revierte automáticamente.

safety_rollback_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that wraps every execution in a transaction and rolls it back afterwards.

safety_select_only_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Block all but SELECT” checkbox; INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and any other non-SELECT statement is refused.
safety_select_only_description.value: Bloquear INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE y otras instrucciones que no sean SELECT.

safety_select_only_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that only allows SELECT queries; SQL keywords stay untranslated.

safety_touch_connect_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require Touch ID to connect” checkbox; a Touch ID fingerprint check is needed before the connection opens.
safety_touch_connect_description.value: Requerir Touch ID antes de conectarse.

safety_touch_connect_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) requiring a Touch ID fingerprint check before connecting; Touch ID is Apple’s product name.

safety_touch_non_select_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require Touch ID for non-SELECT” checkbox; a Touch ID check is needed before running any statement other than SELECT.
safety_touch_non_select_description.value: Requerir Touch ID antes de ejecutar instrucciones que no sean SELECT.

safety_touch_non_select_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) requiring a Touch ID check before any non-SELECT statement runs.
safety_touch_non_select_label.value: Requerir Touch ID para instrucciones que no sean SELECT

safety_unbounded_delete_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Allow unconstrained DELETE” checkbox; a DELETE with no WHERE clause runs without the usual extra confirmation.
safety_unbounded_delete_description.value: Permitir DELETE sin una cláusula WHERE y sin confirmación adicional.

safety_unbounded_delete_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that lets DELETE statements without a WHERE clause run without an extra warning.

safety_unbounded_update_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Allow unconstrained UPDATE” checkbox; an UPDATE with no WHERE clause runs without the usual extra confirmation.
safety_unbounded_update_description.value: Permitir UPDATE sin una cláusula WHERE y sin confirmación adicional.

safety_unbounded_update_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that lets UPDATE statements without a WHERE clause run without an extra warning.

save_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Footer: primary button at the bottom right that saves the name, color, icon and query protections of the selected entry.

saved_named.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after Save succeeds; {entity_name} is the saved client, project or environment name.

select_icon_title.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Icon → Browse…: title of the native file picker window opened to choose an icon image.

untitled_row.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: fallback text shown for a client, project or environment whose name is blank.

account_registration_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when sign-in succeeded but the account could not be added to SQLLY’s list of Entra accounts; {error} is the technical reason.
account_registration_failed.value: No se pudo registrar la cuenta de Microsoft Entra: {error}

account_removed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: green confirmation after the second click on Confirm removal deletes an account; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.

add_user.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: primary button that opens the web browser to sign in a new Microsoft Entra account; replaced by “Signing in…” while that is in progress.

browser_signin_unavailable.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail in the browser version when Add User is clicked, because Microsoft Entra sign-in cannot run inside a web page.
browser_signin_unavailable.value: El inicio de sesión en Microsoft Entra no está disponible

confirm_removal.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: red label the Remove button switches to after its first click; clicking again permanently signs the selected account out, Escape cancels.

dialog_subtitle.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Header: grey one-line description next to the Entra icon at the top of the dialog body, explaining the list shows signed-in accounts usable by connections.
dialog_subtitle.value: Cuentas con sesión iniciada disponibles para la gestión de conexiones.

dialog_title.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Title bar: title bar of the dialog that lists, adds, refreshes and removes Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) accounts used for database sign-in.

empty_accounts.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: centered empty-state text when no Entra accounts are signed in yet, pointing the user to the Add User button.
empty_accounts.value: Aún no hay cuentas; elige Añadir usuario para iniciar sesión con Microsoft Entra.

fallback_account_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row when neither its user name nor its tenant ID is known.

keychain_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the account’s sign-in tokens could not be stored in the operating system keychain; {error} is the technical reason.
keychain_failed.value: No se pudieron guardar los tokens de Microsoft Entra en el llavero del sistema: {error}

oauth_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the browser-based Microsoft sign-in itself fails or is cancelled; {error} is the reason returned.
oauth_failed.value: Error al iniciar sesión con Microsoft Entra: {error}

preview_browser_banner.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Banner: notice at the top of the dialog in the public web demo, saying the accounts shown are examples and real accounts must be added in the desktop app.
preview_browser_banner.value: Solo con fines ilustrativos: la vista previa web no puede iniciar sesión con Microsoft Entra ni acceder a Azure. Usa la aplicación de escritorio para añadir cuentas reales.

refresh_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: small button at the right of each account row that re-runs browser sign-in to renew that account’s expired credentials.

refreshing_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: label that replaces the Refresh button on the one row whose credentials are being renewed.

remove_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: button beside Add User that starts removing the selected account; the first click asks for confirmation.

remove_confirmation.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: confirmation prompt after the first click on Remove, explaining what removal does; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.
remove_confirmation.value: ¿Eliminar {account_label}? Se cerrará la sesión de esta cuenta en SQLLY en este equipo. Tu cuenta de Microsoft no se verá afectada.

served_browser_banner.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Banner: notice at the top of the dialog when SQLLY runs in a browser served by an organization, saying Entra sign-in is unavailable and an administrator sets up such connections.
served_browser_banner.value: SQLLY en el navegador no puede iniciar sesión en Microsoft Entra. Las conexiones que necesitan una cuenta de Entra las configura tu administrador.

signin_coordination_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the background sign-in task stops unexpectedly before finishing; {error} is the technical reason.
signin_coordination_failed.value: No se pudo coordinar el inicio de sesión con Microsoft Entra: {error}

signin_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: red error after adding or refreshing an account fails, shown with a Try again button; {error} is the specific failure reason.

signin_succeeded.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: green confirmation after browser sign-in finishes and the account is added or refreshed; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.
signin_succeeded.value: Sesión iniciada como {account_label}. Tokens guardados en el llavero del sistema operativo.

signing_in.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: disabled label that replaces the Add User button while a browser sign-in is in progress.

tenant_only_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row when only the tenant is known; {tenant_id} is the Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID.

tokens_in_keychain.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: default grey note when the dialog opens or an action is cancelled, reassuring that sign-in tokens are kept in the operating system keychain.
tokens_in_keychain.value: Los tokens permanecen en el llavero del sistema operativo.

try_again.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: button to the right of a sign-in error that repeats the failed add or refresh attempt.

untitled_user.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list and status line: fallback name for an account that has neither a display name nor a user name.

username_tenant_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row; {username} is the sign-in name and {tenant_id} the Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID, separated by a bullet.

waiting_for_refresh.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: progress message after clicking Refresh on a row while the browser sign-in to renew that account is open; {account_label} is the account’s name.
waiting_for_refresh.value: Esperando a que termines de iniciar sesión en tu navegador para actualizar {account_label}.

waiting_for_signin.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: progress message after clicking Add User while the user completes the Microsoft Entra sign-in in their web browser.
waiting_for_signin.value: Esperando a que termines de iniciar sesión con Microsoft Entra en tu navegador.

add_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: primary button, enabled while the rule form is editable, that sends the rule name and address range to Azure to create or update the server firewall rule.

address_help.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: small dimmed help line under the Start IP and End IP fields explaining that equal addresses allow a single IP and that an existing rule name is overwritten.
address_help.value: Deja ambas direcciones iguales para permitir solo esta IP. Reutilizar un nombre de regla actualiza esa regla en lugar de añadir otra.

applied_body.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result: success message replacing the form after Azure accepts the rule; {server} is the server host name, {range} the single IP or start–end range, {rule_name} the rule; warns that reconnecting may fail for a few minutes.

cancel_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: secondary button beside Add Firewall Rule that dismisses the prompt without contacting Azure; disabled while the request is in flight.

close_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: only button left once the dialog shows a final result or explains it cannot add the rule; closes the dialog.

contacting_azure.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: dimmed progress text under the form while the firewall rule request is being sent to Azure and the form is locked.

dialog_title.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Title bar: dialog title, shown when an Azure SQL server refuses the connection (error 40615) because the client IP is not on its firewall allow-list.
dialog_title.value: El firewall del servidor está bloqueando tu IP

end_ip_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the input for the last IPv4 address of the range to allow (prefilled with the blocked IP; label column is narrow).

flow_account_not_registered.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: explanation shown instead of the form when the connection’s Microsoft Entra account was never signed in on this machine; points to the Azure SQL Connection… menu item to sign in.
flow_account_not_registered.value: La cuenta de Microsoft Entra del perfil activo no está registrada. Inicia sesión mediante Conexión de Azure SQL… y vuelve a intentarlo.

flow_applied.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: success message after the Tools-menu command looked up your public IP and added a rule; {server_fqdn} is the server, {range} the IP or range, {rule_name} the generated rule name.

flow_failed.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: generic failure message when Azure or the token refresh returns an unclassified error; {error} is the underlying error detail shown on the following lines.
flow_failed.value:
No se pudo añadir la regla de firewall.

{error}

flow_forbidden.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when Azure answers 403 because the signed-in account lacks permission to write firewall rules on {server_fqdn}; tells the user to ask an Azure administrator.
flow_forbidden.value:
No parece que tengas permiso para cambiar el firewall de {server_fqdn}.

Azure rechazó el cambio porque la cuenta con la que iniciaste sesión no tiene el permiso Microsoft.Sql/servers/firewallRules/write en este servidor. Tendrás que pedir a alguien que sí lo tenga (un administrador de Azure o cualquier persona con el rol SQL Server Contributor en el servidor) que añada la regla por ti o que te conceda ese permiso.

flow_ip_lookup_failed.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the Tools-menu command cannot learn your public IPv4 from the api.ipify.org echo service; {error} is the network error detail; suggests adding the IP in the Azure portal.

flow_no_entra_binding.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error shown when the active connection has no Microsoft Entra account attached (for example it uses SQL authentication), so there is no Azure credential to change the firewall with.
flow_no_entra_binding.value: La cuenta de Microsoft Entra del perfil activo no está en la lista de cuentas registradas. Inicia sesión mediante Conexión de Azure SQL… y vuelve a intentarlo.

flow_no_subscriptions.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the signed-in Azure account can see no subscriptions at all, so the server cannot be located to add the rule.
flow_no_subscriptions.value: La cuenta con la que iniciaste sesión no puede acceder a ninguna suscripción de Azure. Inicia sesión con una cuenta que tenga acceso a la suscripción del servidor.

flow_not_azure_profile.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error for when the active connection is not an Azure SQL server host (*.database.windows.net or *.database.azure.com); asks the user to connect to one first.
flow_not_azure_profile.value: El perfil activo no es un servidor de Azure SQL. Conéctate a un servidor *.database.windows.net (o *.database.azure.com) y vuelve a intentarlo.

flow_server_not_found.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when {server_fqdn} (the server host name) is not found in any Azure subscription the signed-in account can read; suggests checking tenant and Reader access.
flow_server_not_found.value: No se encontró {server_fqdn} en ninguna suscripción de Azure accesible para la cuenta con la que iniciaste sesión. Confirma que iniciaste sesión en el inquilino correcto y que tienes al menos acceso Reader a la suscripción del servidor.

flow_signin_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the cached Microsoft Entra sign-in is missing or expired and cannot be refreshed silently; tells the user to sign in again via Azure SQL Connection….
flow_signin_required.value: El inicio de sesión con Microsoft Entra es obligatorio o ha caducado. Usa Conexión de Azure SQL… para iniciar sesión y vuelve a intentarlo.

prompt_with_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when the server’s error did not name the blocked client IP but the signing-in Azure account is known; {server} is the server, {account} the account name.
prompt_with_account.value: El servidor de Azure SQL {server} rechazó la conexión porque la IP de tu cliente no está en la lista de permitidos de su firewall (error 40615). SQLLY puede añadir una regla de firewall para esa dirección mediante tu cuenta de Azure con sesión iniciada ({account}), que necesita permiso para cambiar el firewall de este servidor. No se enviará nada a Azure hasta que elijas Añadir regla de firewall.

prompt_with_ip.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when the server named the blocked IP but the Azure account name is unknown; {server} is the server, {client_ip} the refused address.
prompt_with_ip.value: El servidor de Azure SQL {server} rechazó la conexión porque la IP de tu cliente ({client_ip}) no está en la lista de permitidos de su firewall (error 40615). SQLLY puede añadir una regla de firewall para esa dirección mediante tu cuenta de Azure con sesión iniciada. No se enviará nada a Azure hasta que elijas Añadir regla de firewall.

prompt_with_ip_and_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when both the blocked client IP and the Azure account are known; {server} is the server, {client_ip} the refused address, {account} the account name.
prompt_with_ip_and_account.value: El servidor de Azure SQL {server} rechazó la conexión porque la IP de tu cliente ({client_ip}) no está en la lista de permitidos de su firewall (error 40615). SQLLY puede añadir una regla de firewall para esa dirección mediante tu cuenta de Azure con sesión iniciada ({account}), que necesita permiso para cambiar el firewall de este servidor. No se enviará nada a Azure hasta que elijas Añadir regla de firewall.

prompt_without_ip_or_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when neither the blocked client IP nor the Azure account name is known; {server} is the Azure SQL server host name.
prompt_without_ip_or_account.value: El servidor de Azure SQL {server} rechazó la conexión porque la IP de tu cliente no está en la lista de permitidos de su firewall (error 40615). SQLLY puede añadir una regla de firewall para esa dirección mediante tu cuenta de Azure con sesión iniciada. No se enviará nada a Azure hasta que elijas Añadir regla de firewall.

public_ip_network_error.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error detail inserted into the “could not determine your public IP” message when the request to the IP echo service fails; {endpoint} is the service URL, {error} the network error.
public_ip_network_error.value: Error de red al contactar con {endpoint}: {error}

rule_name_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the first input, holding the Azure firewall rule name (prefilled like SQLLY-user-date); label column is narrow.

start_ip_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the input for the first IPv4 address of the range to allow (prefilled with the blocked IP; label column is narrow).

token_refresh_failed.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error detail placed inside the generic failure message when silently renewing the Microsoft Entra access token fails; {error} is the token service error.
token_refresh_failed.value: No se pudo actualizar el token de acceso de Entra: {error}

validation_ipv4_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when Start IP or End IP is not a valid dotted IPv4 address.

validation_name_characters.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the rule name contains characters other than letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.
validation_name_characters.value: Los nombres de regla pueden usar solo letras, dígitos, guiones y guiones bajos.

validation_name_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule with the Rule name field empty.
validation_name_required.value: Introduce un nombre para la regla de firewall.

validation_name_too_long.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the rule name exceeds Azure’s 128-character limit.
validation_name_too_long.value: El nombre de la regla supera los 128 caracteres permitidos por Azure.

validation_range_order.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the Start IP is numerically higher than the End IP.
validation_range_order.value: La dirección de inicio no debe ser mayor que la dirección de finalización.

by_client.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by their Client field (the overflow menu currently shows the shorter “By client” label).

by_environment.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by environment (Production, Staging and so on); title-case menu-item style.

by_project.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by their Project field; title-case menu-item style.

by_server.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by server name; title-case menu-item style.

no_grouping.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the default mode that lists connections flat with no group folders (the overflow menu shows it as “All”).

unassigned.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections tree: name of the group folder, always sorted last, that collects connections with no value for the active grouping (no client, project, environment or server set).

authenticity_message.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Body: first line, shown when an SSH tunnel reaches a server whose key is not in known_hosts; {host} is the SSH host name and {port} its port number.
authenticity_message.value: No se puede comprobar la autenticidad del host {host}:{port}.

cancel_button.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Footer: secondary button that rejects the unfamiliar host key and aborts the SSH tunnel connection.

fingerprint_message.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Body: second line in monospace under the warning; {key_type} is the key algorithm (for example ssh-ed25519) and {fingerprint} the SHA256 fingerprint to verify.
fingerprint_message.value: La huella digital de la clave {key_type} es SHA256:{fingerprint}

title.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Title bar: dialog title shown when connecting through an SSH tunnel to a host whose key is not yet trusted in known_hosts.

trust_button.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Footer: primary button that trusts the shown host key (saving it to known_hosts) and continues the connection.

title.location: SSH verification dialog → Title bar: dialog title shown when an SSH tunnel's server accepted the key or password and now asks for more sign-in information such as a one-time code.

server_message.location: SSH verification dialog → Body: first line naming the SSH account and server that is asking for more sign-in information; {username}, {host} and {port} are the SSH user, server and port.
server_message.value: {username}@{host}:{port} pide más datos para iniciar sesión.

not_saved_note.location: SSH verification dialog → Body: small note under the answer fields explaining that the codes typed are sent once and not stored.
not_saved_note.value: Lo que escribas aquí se envía al servidor una sola vez y nunca se guarda.

continue_button.location: SSH verification dialog → Footer: primary button that sends the typed answers (for example a one-time code) to the SSH server.

cancel_button.location: SSH verification dialog → Footer: secondary button that stops the sign-in without sending any answer; the connection fails.

discovery_failed.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: error under the section when a Refresh button’s kubectl lookup of contexts, namespaces or targets fails to run; {error} is the system or exit error.
discovery_failed.value: Error en la detección de Kubernetes: {error}

discovery_timed_out.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: error under the section when the kubectl lookup started by a Refresh button gets no answer within 10 seconds.
discovery_timed_out.value: La detección de Kubernetes agotó el tiempo de espera tras 10 segundos.

kubectl_not_found.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: dimmed notice under the section, also returned by Refresh, when no kubectl program is on PATH or configured; names the Preferences setting to set it.
kubectl_not_found.value: No se encontró kubectl en PATH. Instala kubectl o configura su ubicación en Preferencias → Avanzado → Kubernetes.

account_password_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → SQL account details: placeholder in the masked Password input of a saved SQL login account (not the connection form’s password field); a lowercase hint word.

accounts_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Accounts pane, where Microsoft Entra and saved SQL login accounts are managed; short plural noun.

add_connection_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text beside the Connect button after the + button clears the form to start a new connection.

add_entra_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list footer: button that starts a browser sign-in to register a new Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) account.

add_sql_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list footer: very short button next to the Entra button that clears the details form to create a new saved SQL login account; “+” means add.

advanced_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: heading of the last settings group, holding the connect timeout, query timeout, and startup SQL fields.

appearance_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor: heading of the group holding the Color picker and Icon drop zone for the selected client, project, or environment.

auth_mode_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the segmented control that picks the sign-in method (SQL login, Windows, Microsoft Entra, IAM, token).

auth_token_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text under the Auth token field, shown when the engine signs in with a token instead of a username and password.
auth_token_hint.value: Pega el token de la base de datos o el JWT; déjalo en blanco para un servidor local sin autenticación. Se guarda en el llavero del sistema.

auth_token_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the masked field for the database access token or JWT, shown for token-based engines.

authentication_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: heading of the settings group that holds the sign-in mode and credential fields.

aws_iam_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text shown when AWS RDS IAM sign-in is chosen, explaining the required AWS CLI login and the 15-minute token; keep the commands in backticks untranslated.
aws_iam_hint.value: Requiere `aws sso login` o `aws configure`; el token se genera al conectar y dura 15 minutos.

aws_profile_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the dropdown choosing which local AWS CLI profile mints the RDS IAM token (desktop only).

azure_listing_manual_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: note under the Azure server field when SQLLY could not list the account’s Azure SQL servers (often missing permission), telling the user to type the name.
azure_listing_manual_hint.value: SQLLY no pudo enumerar tus servidores de Azure SQL; escribe el nombre del servidor arriba.

azure_permission_copied.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: confirmation under the Azure server field after the info button copies a Reader-role request for the user’s admin to the clipboard.
azure_permission_copied.value: Para enumerar servidores se necesita el rol Reader en la suscripción (Microsoft.Sql/servers/read). Se copió al portapapeles un mensaje que puedes compartir con tu administrador.

azure_permission_request.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Azure server field info button: clipboard text copied by the info button beside the Azure server field: a first-person request to an Azure admin asking for the Reader role; {account_label} is the user’s Entra account name.
azure_permission_request.value: Por favor, concede a mi cuenta «{account_label}» el rol Reader en la suscripción para que pueda encontrar los servidores a los que tengo acceso sin tener que escribirlos a mano

azure_servers_loading.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: loading text inside the Azure SQL server dropdown while the servers for the chosen Microsoft Entra account are fetched.

binding_account_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: small caption above the list of registered Microsoft Entra accounts, shown when Entra sign-in is chosen; the user picks which account to use.

browser_icon_picker_unavailable.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: message shown in the browser (web) version when Choose File… is clicked for an icon, because no file picker is available there.
browser_icon_picker_unavailable.value: Elegir un archivo de icono no está disponible cuando SQLLY se ejecuta en un navegador

browser_preview_banner.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Top banner: notice shown in the browser (web) preview explaining it uses a bundled sample database and cannot reach real SQL Server instances.
browser_preview_banner.value: Solo con fines ilustrativos: la vista previa web no puede acceder a SQL Server. Se ejecuta con una base de datos de muestra incluida; usa la aplicación de escritorio para conectarte a servidores reales.

ca_file_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: label of the path field (with Browse button) for the certificate-authority file used to verify the server’s TLS certificate; PostgreSQL/MySQL only.

certificate_file_filter.location: Choose certificate file dialog → File-type filter: filter name for .pem, .crt, .cer, and .key files in the file chooser opened from Browse beside the TLS file fields.

choose_file_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Appearance group → Icon: button inside the icon drop zone that opens a file picker to select an image for the client, project, or environment.

client_certificate_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: label of the path field for the client TLS certificate file presented to the server (mutual TLS); PostgreSQL/MySQL only.

client_key_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: label of the path field for the private key file that pairs with the client TLS certificate; PostgreSQL/MySQL only.

client_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: label of the dropdown assigning the connection to a client (a customer or organization defined in the Clients pane).

clients_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Clients pane for managing clients (customers/organizations) used to group connections.

close_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: rightmost button that closes the dialog; with unsaved edits it first shows the Save / Discard / Keep editing prompt.

color_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Appearance group: label of the color picker that sets the tint for the selected client, project, or environment.

connect_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: button that saves the connection form and opens a connection to that server.

connection_failed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Test result: red result line below the form after Test fails or the Microsoft Entra token cannot be obtained; {error} is the failure reason.

connection_name_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: placeholder in the Name input, where the user types a display name for the connection.

connection_not_found.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: error status when duplicating a connection whose saved profile no longer exists.

connection_string_filled.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after a pasted connection string or URL was applied to fill the form fields.
connection_string_filled.value: Campos completados desde la cadena de conexión

connection_string_filled_ignored.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after a pasted connection string filled the form but some options were not understood; {ignored_count} is the number of skipped options.
connection_string_filled_ignored.value: Campos completados desde la cadena de conexión; se ignoraron {ignored_count} opciones

connection_string_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: label of the input revealed by the Paste URL button, where a URL, ADO.NET, or JDBC connection string is pasted to fill the form.

connection_string_read_failed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: error status when a pasted connection string cannot be parsed; {error} explains why.
connection_string_read_failed.value: No se pudo leer la cadena de conexión: {error}

connection_successful.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Test result: green result line below the form after Test connects successfully.

connections_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Connections pane (saved connection list plus the connection form).

copy_azure_permission_tooltip.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: tooltip on the info icon beside the Azure listing note; clicking copies a request for the Azure Reader role.
copy_azure_permission_tooltip.value: Copiar la solicitud de permiso Reader de Azure

credentials_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: row label shown instead of the sign-in mode picker for file-based engines (e.g. SQLite), above a note that no credentials are needed.

database_engine_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: label of the dropdown selecting the database engine (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.).

database_file_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: label replacing Host for file-based engines such as SQLite or DuckDB, where the user enters the database file path.

database_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: label of the field (with a dropdown caret listing the server’s databases) for the default database to open.

database_password_load_failed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Database dropdown: red error inside the database list when the saved SQL account password cannot be read from the keychain; {error} is the reason.
database_password_load_failed.value: No se pudo cargar la contraseña de la cuenta SQL: {error}

database_user_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the database user name field shown when AWS RDS IAM sign-in is chosen.
database_user_label.value: Usuario de la base de datos

databases_loading.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Database dropdown: loading text inside the dropdown while the server’s database names are fetched.

deleted_profile.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after the − button deletes a saved connection; {profile_name} is the deleted connection’s name.

detached_window_title.location: Connections & Settings popped-out window → Title bar: operating-system window title used when the dialog is detached into its own window.

dev_environment.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: group heading in the connection tree for connections in the DEV (development) environment tier; short all-caps tag.

dialog_title.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Title bar (no unsaved edits): dialog title bar text shown when there are no unsaved edits.

dialog_title_edited.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Title bar (unsaved edits): dialog title bar text while the connection form has unsaved edits; the suffix signals pending changes.

discard_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Unsaved-changes prompt: red button in the footer prompt (shown when closing with unsaved edits) that throws the edits away and closes.

discovered_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small badge on an Azure SQL database row found via Microsoft Entra discovery that is not yet linked to a saved connection.

drop_icon_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Appearance group → Icon: main text in the icon drop zone inviting the user to drag an image file onto it.
drop_icon_hint.value: Suelta aquí una imagen de icono

duplicate_created.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after the duplicate button loads an unsaved copy of a connection into the form; {profile_name} is the original connection’s name.
duplicate_created.value: Copia de «{profile_name}»: ajústala y haz clic en Guardar para añadirla junto a la original.

duplicate_password_missing.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: warning status after duplicating a connection when the original’s saved password could not be read, so the copy has an empty password; {profile_name} is the original.
duplicate_password_missing.value: Copia de «{profile_name}»: no se pudo leer la contraseña original del llavero del sistema; introduce una contraseña y haz clic en Guardar.

editing_profile.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after selecting a saved connection in the list loads it into the form; {profile_name} is the connection’s name.

empty_clients.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients pane → List: empty-state text in the client list when no clients have been created.

empty_environments.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Environments pane → List: empty-state text in the environment list when no environments have been created.

empty_projects.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Projects pane → List: empty-state text in the project list when no projects have been created.

encrypt_connection_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: checkbox label to encrypt traffic with TLS, shown for SQL Server-style engines; locked on when the engine or IAM sign-in requires TLS.

enforced_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: short right-aligned tag on a safety rule forced on by the connection’s client, project, or environment, meaning it cannot be turned off here.

enter_server_first.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Database dropdown: message inside the database list when it is opened before a host is entered.

entering_credentials_directly.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after clicking the already-selected saved SQL account chip again, releasing the username and password fields for manual entry.

entity_name_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Details group: label of the name field for the selected client, project, or environment.

entity_name_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Details group: placeholder in the name input for a client, project, or environment.

entity_name_required.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: validation message when Save is clicked with an empty client, project, or environment name.

entity_removed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: short confirmation after the − button deletes the selected client, project, or environment.

entity_saved.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: confirmation after saving a client, project, or environment; {entity_name} is its name.

entra_account_detail_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account details: heading of the read-only details group shown when a Microsoft Entra account is selected in the list.

entra_account_name_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Microsoft Entra account details: row label for the account’s friendly display name.

entra_account_tenant_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Microsoft Entra account details: row label for the Azure tenant (directory) ID the account belongs to.

entra_account_username_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Microsoft Entra account details: row label for the account’s sign-in user name (email).

entra_complete_browser_signin.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Status line: message shown while the Microsoft Entra browser sign-in is in progress, asking the user to finish it in the browser.
entra_complete_browser_signin.value: Termina de iniciar sesión en tu navegador para registrar tu cuenta de Microsoft Entra.

entra_credentials_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text shown when Microsoft Entra sign-in is chosen, explaining tokens come from the system Entra token cache.
entra_credentials_hint.value: Las credenciales se obtienen de la caché de tokens de Microsoft Entra del sistema.

entra_initial_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Status line: initial guidance shown before any Microsoft Entra account is signed in during this session.
entra_initial_status.value: Inicia sesión para registrar una cuenta de Microsoft Entra (Azure AD).

entra_list_header.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list: small section header above the Microsoft Entra accounts; product name, normally left untranslated.

entra_removed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Status line: confirmation after Remove deletes a Microsoft Entra account; {account_label} is the account’s display name or email.

entra_signed_in.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Status line: confirmation after the browser sign-in succeeds and the account is registered; {account_label} is the account’s display name or email.

entra_signin_failed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Status line: error after the Microsoft Entra browser sign-in fails; {error} is the reason.

entra_signing_in_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list footer: disabled label replacing Add Microsoft Entra Account while a browser sign-in is in progress.

environment_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: label of the segmented control choosing the connection’s environment tier (PROD, STAGE, TEST, DEV, LOCAL).

environments_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Environments pane for managing named environments with their own color, icon, and safety rules.

failed_badge.location: Connection Management → Connections → Health: badge for a failed connection test.

favorite_added.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after the Favorite button marks the connection as a favorite; {profile_name} is the connection’s name.

favorite_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: button that marks the selected saved connection as a favorite; the star symbol is part of the label.

favorite_removed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after the Unfavorite button removes the connection from favorites; {profile_name} is the connection’s name.

filter_connections_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: placeholder in the search box above the connection tree that filters it by name.

fix_validation_before_connect.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text when Connect is clicked while the form still has validation errors.
fix_validation_before_connect.value: Corrige los errores de validación antes de conectarte.

fix_validation_before_save.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text when Save is clicked while the form still has validation errors.
fix_validation_before_save.value: Corrige los errores de validación antes de guardar.

fix_validation_before_test.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text when Test is clicked while the form still has validation errors.
fix_validation_before_test.value: Corrige los errores de validación antes de probar.

gcp_adc_check_again.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: small button under the Google Cloud credentials status that re-checks for Application Default Credentials (GCP Cloud SQL IAM).

gcp_adc_check_failed.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: status line when the background check for Google Cloud Application Default Credentials could not run at all.
gcp_adc_check_failed.value: No se pudieron comprobar Application Default Credentials

gcp_adc_checking.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: status line shown while SQLLY checks for Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (GCP Cloud SQL IAM sign-in).

gcp_adc_error.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: status line when the Google Cloud Application Default Credentials check returns an error; {error} is the reason.
gcp_adc_error.value: No se pudieron comprobar Application Default Credentials: {error}

gcp_adc_found.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: status line confirming Google Cloud Application Default Credentials were found, so Cloud SQL IAM sign-in can proceed.

gcp_iam_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text shown when GCP Cloud SQL IAM sign-in is chosen, naming the required gcloud login; keep the backticked command untranslated.
gcp_iam_hint.value: Requiere Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`); el token se genera al conectarse.

health_days_ago.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: relative time of the last connection test, in days; {count} is the number of days; very short abbreviation.

health_hours_ago.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: relative time of the last connection test, in hours; {count} is the number of hours; very short abbreviation.

health_just_now.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: relative time used when the last connection test was under a minute ago; follows a status word and a separator dot.

health_minutes_ago.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: relative time of the last connection test, in minutes; {count} is the number of minutes; very short abbreviation.

health_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: heading of the group showing the last test result for a saved connection, shown only when editing a saved connection.

health_with_error.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: summary line joining {status} (Healthy/Failed/Untested), {observed} (when last tested), and {error} (the last error) with dots.

health_without_error.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: summary line joining {status} (Healthy/Failed/Untested) and {observed} (when last tested) when no error was recorded.

healthy_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small green badge on a saved connection whose last test succeeded; also the status word in the Connection health summary.

host_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: label of the server host name or IP address field for network database engines.

iam_tls_note.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: note under the TLS settings when AWS or GCP IAM sign-in is chosen, explaining encryption is always on.
iam_tls_note.value: El inicio de sesión con IAM siempre usa TLS

iam_user_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the IAM user or service-account name field shown for GCP Cloud SQL IAM sign-in.

icon_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Appearance group: row label for the icon drop zone where an image is chosen for the client, project, or environment.

icon_selected.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: confirmation after an icon image is dropped or chosen; {path} is the image file path.

image_file_filter.location: Select icon file dialog → File-type filter: filter name for image files (PNG, JPEG, SVG, etc.) in the chooser opened from Choose File… in the client/project/environment Icon area.

inherited_safety.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: row describing a safety rule forced on by an assigned client, project, or environment; {flag_label} is the rule name, {source_name} is the entity’s name.

initial_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text shown when the dialog first opens, before any connection is selected or created.
initial_status.value: Añade una nueva conexión o selecciona una para editarla.

invalid_host.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: red inline error under the Host field when the text is not a valid IP address, host name, or *.domain wildcard.
invalid_host.value: No es una IP, un nombre de host o un comodín *.domain válido.

invalid_instance.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: red inline error under the Host field when the SQL Server instance name after the backslash is invalid.
invalid_instance.value: El nombre de la instancia no es válido.

keep_editing_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Unsaved-changes prompt: button in the footer prompt that dismisses the prompt and returns to the form without closing.

keep_editing_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text after Keep editing is chosen in the unsaved-changes prompt, reminding that the edits are still there.
keep_editing_status.value: Sigues editando: no se descartó nada.

last_observed_status_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Connection health group: row label above the health summary line (status, when tested, last error) for the saved connection.

linked_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small badge on an Azure SQL database row found via Microsoft Entra discovery that already matches a saved connection.

local_environment.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: group heading in the connection tree for connections in the LOCAL environment tier (local development machine); short all-caps tag.

name_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: field label for the connection’s display name, the name shown in the connection list and pickers.

never_tested.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Health group → Last observed status: lowercase fragment filling the time slot of “{status} · {observed}” when the connection has never been tested.

new_client.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients pane → Client editor: default name pre-filled in the Name field after clicking the + button below the client list to start a new client.

new_client_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients pane → Footer status line: status shown beside Save after clicking + to start a new client, meaning the editor holds an unsaved new client.
new_client_status.value: Nuevo cliente: ponle un nombre y haz clic en Guardar.

new_environment.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Environments pane → Environment editor: default name pre-filled in the Name field after clicking the + button below the environment list.

new_environment_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Environments pane → Footer status line: status shown beside Save after clicking + to start a new environment, meaning the editor holds an unsaved new environment.
new_environment_status.value: Nuevo entorno: ponle un nombre y haz clic en Guardar.

new_project.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Projects pane → Project editor: default name pre-filled in the Name field after clicking the + button below the project list.

new_project_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Projects pane → Footer status line: status shown beside Save after clicking + to start a new project, meaning the editor holds an unsaved new project.
new_project_status.value: Nuevo proyecto: ponle un nombre y haz clic en Guardar.

new_sql_account_detail_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account editor: group heading above the Name, Username and Password fields while creating a new reusable SQL login (no saved SQL account selected).

no_azure_servers.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host dropdown (Microsoft Entra mode): empty-state message in the Azure SQL server list when the bound Entra account can see no servers; the host can still be typed.
no_azure_servers.value: No se encontraron servidores de Azure SQL accesibles. Aún puedes introducir un servidor manualmente.

no_color.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Appearance group → Color row: text beside the color picker when the selected client, project or environment has no color set.

no_connections.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: empty-state message in the saved-connection tree when it has no rows and the search box above it is empty.

no_databases.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Database dropdown: empty-state message in the dropdown opened by the caret beside the Database field when the server returns no databases.

no_entity_choice.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group → Client and Project dropdowns: placeholder and first option meaning no client or project is assigned; choosing it clears the assignment.

no_entra_accounts.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list → Microsoft Entra section: empty-state row under the “Microsoft Entra” header when no Entra accounts have been added yet.
no_entra_accounts.value: No hay cuentas de Entra registradas todavía.

no_entra_bindings.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group (Microsoft Entra mode): note shown where account choices would be listed when no Entra accounts are registered to bind this connection to.
no_entra_bindings.value: No hay vinculaciones de cuentas de Microsoft Entra

no_filtered_connections.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: empty-state message in the saved-connection tree when text typed in the search box above it matches no connection.
no_filtered_connections.value: Ninguna conexión coincide con el filtro.

no_query_timeout_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Advanced group → Query timeout (seconds) field: placeholder shown when the field is empty, meaning queries run without a time limit.

no_saved_sql_accounts.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group (SQL login mode): note above Username/Password when no reusable SQL accounts exist; points to the Accounts pane or typing credentials directly.
no_saved_sql_accounts.value: No hay cuentas SQL guardadas. Añade una en la sección Cuentas o introduce las credenciales abajo.

no_sql_accounts.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list → SQL authentication section: empty-state row under the “SQL authentication” header when no reusable SQL logins have been saved yet.
no_sql_accounts.value: Aún no hay cuentas de autenticación SQL.

no_testable_connections.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Test All when no saved connection can be tested unattended, because sign-in (Entra) and cloud IAM connections are skipped.
no_testable_connections.value: No hay conexiones guardadas que se puedan probar (se omiten las conexiones de inicio de sesión y de IAM en la nube).

optional_database_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Database field: placeholder indicating a database name is optional; leaving it empty uses the server’s default database.

organization_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: group heading at the top of the form above the Name, Database engine, Client, Project and Environment rows.

password_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group (SQL login mode): field label for the login password, below Username; locked when a saved SQL account supplies the credentials.

password_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: lowercase placeholder in the masked Password input (also the Auth token input for token engines) when it is empty.

paste_url_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: small button at the top of the group that shows or hides a Connection string field where a pasted URL or connection string fills in the form.

port_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group: field label for the network port number, below Host; the field is disabled for file-based engines such as SQLite.

production_environment.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: group node for the production environment level (below client and project) grouping connections marked as production; all-caps tag.

project_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Organization group: label of the dropdown that assigns this connection to a project defined in the Projects pane.

projects_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Projects pane, where projects for organizing connections are created and edited.

provisioned_delete_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after trying to delete, with the − button, a connection that was preconfigured from a provisioning file or SQLLY_CONNECTION_ environment variable; explains it is read-only and how to change or copy it.
provisioned_delete_read_only.value: Esta conexión se aprovisiona desde un archivo o desde variables de entorno y aquí es de solo lectura. Edita su definición para cambiarla o duplícala para crear tu propia copia.

provisioned_save_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Save on a connection that was preconfigured from a provisioning file or SQLLY_CONNECTION_ environment variable; explains it is read-only and how to change or copy it.
provisioned_save_read_only.value: Esta conexión se aprovisiona desde un archivo o desde variables de entorno y aquí es de solo lectura. Edita su definición para cambiarla o duplícala para crear tu propia copia.

proxy_browser_banner.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Browser version → Top banner: info banner at the top of the dialog when connections come from the server the browser app runs through and cannot be edited here.
proxy_browser_banner.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_delete_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after trying to delete a connection with the − button in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_delete_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_duplicate_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after trying to duplicate a connection with the ⧉ button in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_duplicate_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_entity_add_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Footer status line: message after clicking + in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_entity_add_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_entity_remove_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Footer status line: message after clicking − in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_entity_remove_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_entity_save_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Save in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_entity_save_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

proxy_save_read_only.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Save on a connection in the browser version when connections come from the server and are read-only.
proxy_save_read_only.value: Estas conexiones se configuran en el servidor a través del que funciona SQLLY y aquí son de solo lectura. Pide a tu administrador que añada o cambie una.

query_timeout_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Advanced group: field label for the per-query time limit in seconds; left empty means no limit. Distinct from the connection timeout above it.
query_timeout_label.value: Tiempo de espera de la consulta (segundos)

region_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group (AWS IAM mode): field label for the AWS region (for example us-west-2) used to mint the RDS IAM sign-in token.

relay_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small lowercase badge on a saved connection row whose traffic is routed through a relay device instead of connecting to the server directly.

remove_entra_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Footer: button shown when a Microsoft Entra account is selected in the list; removes that account from SQLLY.

remove_sql_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Footer: button beside Save Account that deletes the selected reusable SQL login and its keychain password; disabled while creating a new account.

rollback_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small badge on a saved connection row that has “Wrap execution in transaction + rollback” turned on, so its changes are always rolled back.

rollback_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: checkbox label; when on, each execution runs inside a transaction that is rolled back afterwards so no changes persist.
rollback_label.value: Envolver la ejecución en una transacción + rollback

safety_features_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Editor: group heading above safety checkboxes that are forced on for every connection assigned to this item.

safety_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: group heading for TLS/encryption settings and the SELECT-only and rollback-wrap checkboxes, plus safety flags inherited from the client, project or environment.

save_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer: button beside Connect and Close that saves the connection being edited and keeps the dialog open; disabled while the form has validation errors.

save_connection_first.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Favorite when the connection being edited has not been saved yet, so it cannot be starred.

save_entity_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Footer: button that saves the name, appearance and safety settings of the client, project or environment being edited.

save_sql_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Footer: button beside Remove Account that saves the reusable SQL login (name, username, and password to the system keychain).

save_unsaved_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Unsaved changes prompt: button in the footer prompt raised when closing with unsaved connection edits; saves the connection, then closes the dialog.

saved_profile.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: confirmation after the connection is saved; {profile_name} is the connection’s name.

saved_with_secret_warning.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: confirmation after saving a duplicated connection when some passwords could not be copied; {profile_name} is the name, {warning} explains which secrets were not copied.

secret_copy_warning_many.location: Connection Management → Connections → Duplicate connection: warning for multiple unreadable original secrets.
secret_copy_warning_many.value: {count} secretos guardados no se pudieron leer de las entradas del llavero de la conexión original; vuelve a introducirlos en la copia

secret_copy_warning_one.location: Connection Management → Connections → Duplicate connection: warning for one unreadable original secret.
secret_copy_warning_one.value: un secreto guardado no se pudo leer de la entrada del llavero de la conexión original; vuelve a introducirlo en la copia

select_certificate_title.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group → TLS file rows: title of the system file picker opened by Browse… beside the CA file, client certificate or client key path.
select_certificate_title.value: Seleccionar un archivo de certificado o de clave

select_client_to_remove.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients pane → Footer status line: message after clicking − below the client list when no client is selected.

select_connection_to_delete.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking the − button below the connection list when no saved connection is selected to delete.
select_connection_to_delete.value: Selecciona una conexión guardada para eliminarla.

select_connection_to_duplicate.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking the ⧉ duplicate button below the connection list when no saved connection is selected to copy.
select_connection_to_duplicate.value: Selecciona una conexión guardada para duplicarla.

select_connection_to_favorite.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Footer status line: message after clicking Favorite when no saved connection is selected to star.
select_connection_to_favorite.value: Selecciona una conexión guardada para marcarla como favorita.

select_environment_to_remove.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Environments pane → Footer status line: message after clicking − below the environment list when no environment is selected.

select_icon_title.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects or Environments pane → Appearance group → Icon row: title of the system file picker opened by Choose File… to pick an icon image.

select_only_badge.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection list: small badge on a saved connection row that has “Block all but SELECT” turned on, meaning only read queries are allowed; keep SELECT as the SQL keyword.

select_only_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Safety group: checkbox label; when on, the connection refuses any statement other than SELECT. Keep SELECT as the SQL keyword.
