query_completed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a long-running query that finished successfully; shown before the time in the row header.

query_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a long-running query that ended with an error; shown before the time in the row header.

update_available.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a notice that a newer SQLLY version can be installed; shown before the time in the row header.

system_toggle.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: checkbox label in the footer; when checked, SQLLY also posts operating-system notifications for these events while the app is in the background.
system_toggle.value: Notificación del sistema cuando la aplicación esté en segundo plano

tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar: tooltip on the bell icon button at the right of the status bar that opens the Notifications dialog; may show an unread count badge.

copy_license_button.location: Open Source Licenses → License block: button that copies that complete license text to the clipboard.

dependencies_heading.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: section heading above the grouped third-party dependency list.

header.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: main heading above the introduction and dependency catalog.

intro.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: introductory paragraph explaining the dependency list and verbatim license texts.
intro.value: SQLLY se basa en el trabajo de la comunidad de código abierto. A continuación figuran todos los proyectos de terceros de los que depende SQLLY, seguidos del texto completo de cada licencia bajo la que se distribuyen. Cada licencia se reproduce literalmente.

licenses_heading.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: section heading above the full third-party license texts.

used_by.location: Open Source Licenses → License block: line listing the comma-separated dependencies distributed under that license.

window_title.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: native title-bar caption for the third-party dependency and license viewer.

ambiguous_filter_help.location: Open Project File → Filter help: guidance shown for ambiguous s: prefix explaining unambiguous schema and procedure filters.
ambiguous_filter_help.value: Usa schema:, sch:, sproc:, proc: o p: para los filtros de tipo SQL.

browser_demo_banner.location: Open Project File → Illustrative web preview: banner directing users to the desktop app for opening project files from disk.
browser_demo_banner.value: Solo ilustrativo: la vista previa web no puede leer archivos de tu equipo. Usa la aplicación de escritorio para abrir archivos de proyecto desde el disco.

browser_served_banner.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: banner explaining that the browser-hosted application cannot read local files.
browser_served_banner.value: SQLLY en el navegador no puede leer archivos de tu equipo.

choose_folder_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: limitation status shown because browser-hosted SQLLY cannot choose a local project folder.
choose_folder_unavailable.value: No se puede elegir una carpeta de proyecto

choose_root_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that selects a different project root folder.

choose_root_prompt.location: Open Project File → Choose Root: native folder-picker prompt explaining which folder to select.
choose_root_prompt.value: Elige la carpeta que SQLLY debe usar como raíz del proyecto.

copy_path_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that copies the selected file or object path to the clipboard.

create_file_failed.location: Open Project File → New SQL File: error status naming the file that could not be created.

create_file_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: limitation status shown because browser-hosted SQLLY cannot create local files.

data_model_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: source chip identifying an object loaded from the connected data model rather than disk.

ddl_toggle.location: Open Project File → Header: toggle that includes or excludes data-model objects whose definitions can be opened.

dialog_title.location: SQLLY → Open Project File dialog: title for choosing a SQL file or data-model object to open.

filter_placeholder.location: Open Project File → Filter: placeholder describing free-text search and common object and schema filter prefixes.
filter_placeholder.value: Busca archivos o usa v:, p:, f:, schema:

folder_empty.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state title shown when the selected folder has no visible entries.
folder_empty.value: No hay archivos en esta carpeta

folder_empty_detail.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state guidance for adding a SQL file or changing folders.
folder_empty_detail.value: Crea aquí un archivo SQL o navega a otra carpeta.

folder_mode.location: Open Project File → Mode selector: segment that browses one filesystem folder at a time.

folder_path.location: Open Project File → Header: current directory path shown while Folder mode is active.

folder_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state title shown when the current folder cannot be read.

folder_unavailable_detail.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state detail naming the unreadable folder and suggesting recovery steps.
folder_unavailable_detail.value: SQLLY no pudo leer {path}. Elige otra carpeta o comprueba los permisos.

git_button.location: Open Project File → Footer: button that opens Git actions for the current project root.

git_tooltip.location: Open Project File → Footer → Git button: tooltip summarizing the available repository actions.
git_tooltip.value: Estado, diferencias y confirmaciones de Git para esta carpeta del proyecto

hidden_toggle.location: Open Project File → Header: toggle that includes or excludes hidden files and folders.

kind_function.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a function.

kind_index.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for an index.

kind_sproc.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a stored procedure.

kind_table.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a table.

kind_trigger.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a trigger.

kind_type.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a user-defined type.

kind_unknown.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip shown when SQL metadata does not identify an object type.

kind_view.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a view.

load_full_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that reloads a truncated SQL preview without byte or line limits.

loading_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown while loading a newly selected folder.

match_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: chip explaining which localized field or object type matched the active filter.

match_name.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the file name matched the filter.

match_object.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the SQL object name matched the filter.

match_path.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the relative file path matched the filter.

match_schema.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the schema name matched the filter.

multiple_objects_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: metadata chip indicating that a SQL script contains multiple top-level objects.

new_file_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that creates and opens a new SQL file.

no_matches.location: Open Project File → List empty state: title shown when the active filter excludes every scanned row.

no_matches_detail.location: Open Project File → List empty state: guidance for broadening a filter that has no matches.
no_matches_detail.value: Borra el filtro o quita el prefijo para ver más archivos.

open_button.location: Open Project File → Footer: primary button that opens the selected SQL file or data-model definition.

preview_folder_detail.location: Open Project File → Preview → Folder: explanation shown instead of SQL content for a folder selection.
preview_folder_detail.value: Las carpetas no generan vistas previas de SQL.

preview_invalid_utf8.location: Open Project File → Preview: error detail shown when the selected SQL file is not valid UTF-8 text.
preview_invalid_utf8.value: Vista previa no disponible: el archivo no es UTF-8 válido.

preview_missing_title.location: Open Project File → Preview: title shown when the selected SQL file disappeared before it could be loaded.

preview_model_detail.location: Open Project File → Preview → Data-model object: explanation that opening the object fetches its definition from the connected database.
preview_model_detail.value: La definición se obtiene de la base de datos conectada al abrirla (generación de DDL al estilo de sp_helptext).

preview_multiple_objects.location: Open Project File → Preview metadata: note that the script contains several objects and metadata describes only the first.
preview_multiple_objects.value: varios objetos; se muestra el primer objeto de nivel superior

preview_no_selection.location: Open Project File → Preview: title shown when no file or data-model object is selected.

preview_select_file.location: Open Project File → Preview: guidance shown when there is no selection to preview.
preview_select_file.value: Selecciona un archivo SQL para ver su vista previa.

preview_sql_only.location: Open Project File → Preview: explanation shown when the selected file does not have a .sql extension.
preview_sql_only.value: La vista previa solo está disponible para archivos .sql.

preview_truncated.location: Open Project File → Preview metadata: note that displayed SQL was limited by byte or line count.

preview_unreadable.location: Open Project File → Preview: error detail shown when the selected SQL file cannot be read.
preview_unreadable.value: Vista previa no disponible: no se pudo leer el archivo.

project_empty_detail.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state guidance shown when no SQL files are found under the root.
project_empty_detail.value: Cambia al modo Carpeta, elige otra raíz o crea un archivo SQL.

project_empty_title.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state title naming the scanned project root.
project_empty_title.value: No se encontraron archivos SQL en {root_name}

project_mode.location: Open Project File → Mode selector: segment that recursively lists SQL files under the project root.

project_path.location: Open Project File → Header: current project-root path shown while Project SQL mode is active.

project_root_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state title shown when the configured project root does not exist.

project_root_unavailable_detail.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state guidance for recovering from a missing project root.
project_root_unavailable_detail.value: Elige otra raíz del proyecto para usar el modo SQL del proyecto.

refreshing_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown after changing hidden-file visibility.

reveal_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that reveals the selected file in the operating system file manager.

scan_limit.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that recursive scanning stopped at its file limit and guidance for narrowing results.
scan_limit.value: Se alcanzó el límite de archivos de la exploración del proyecto; acota la raíz o filtra los resultados.

scanning_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown after changing the file-browsing mode.

scanning_indicator.location: Open Project File → Header: compact activity indicator shown during a filesystem scan.

scanning_project.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown while recursively scanning the project root.

skipped_folder_plural.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that multiple unreadable folders were skipped.

skipped_folder_singular.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that one unreadable folder was skipped.

skipped_symlink_plural.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that multiple symbolic links escaping the project root were skipped.
skipped_symlink_plural.value: Se omitieron {count} enlaces simbólicos fuera de la raíz del proyecto.

skipped_symlink_singular.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that one symbolic link escaping the project root was skipped.
skipped_symlink_singular.value: Se omitió {count} enlace simbólico fuera de la raíz del proyecto.

source_indexed.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip indicating that scanned metadata also exists in the live schema catalog.

source_scan_only.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip for trigger and index metadata available only from SQL text scanning.

source_scanned.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip indicating that metadata was inferred from SQL file text.

source_unknown.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip shown when no object metadata source is known.

unknown_schema_chip.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: schema chip shown when no schema could be inferred for the selected object.

up_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that navigates to the parent folder without leaving the project boundary.

browser_unavailable.location: Browser version → Query editor → AI summary: phrase naming the unavailable feature, inserted into a “… is not available in the browser” message when an AI query summary is requested.

generate_http_status.location: Query editor → AI summary: error detail when the local AI runtime rejects a summary-generation request; {status} is the HTTP status code and reason, e.g. “500 Internal Server Error”.

http_failed.location: Query editor → AI summary and Settings → AI: error message wrapping a network failure talking to the local AI runtime; {message} is the underlying error text.

invalid_request.location: Query editor → AI summary: short internal error used when a summary is requested with empty SQL or no AI model selected; lowercase fragment.

invalid_response.location: Query editor → AI summary: short error used when the local AI runtime replies with something that cannot be read as a summary; lowercase fragment.

long_pending.location: Tab switcher (Ctrl+Tab) → Tab summary placeholder: placeholder shown under a tab’s name when no AI summary of its query has been generated yet.
long_pending.value: Aún no se ha generado el resumen largo

models_http_status.location: Settings → AI → On device: error detail when checking the local AI runtime’s installed models fails; {status} is the HTTP status code and reason, e.g. “404 Not Found”.

runtime_unreachable_browser.location: Browser version → Settings → AI → On device: phrase inserted into a “… is not available in the browser” message after clicking the check-runtime button; lowercase fragment.
runtime_unreachable_browser.value: no se puede acceder al entorno de ejecución de IA local

short_pending.location: Query editor → AI summary: placeholder meaning the one-line short summary of the tab’s query has not been generated yet; companion of the long-summary placeholder.
short_pending.value: Aún no se ha generado el resumen corto

interval_off.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and first menu option when the query is not re-run automatically; shown only for SELECT-only queries.

interval_one_minute.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and menu option for re-running the query every minute; “1m” is an abbreviation of one minute, keep short.

interval_seconds.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and menu option for re-running the query on a timer; {seconds} is 5, 10 or 30; “s” abbreviates seconds.

accept_inferred_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: small button on a dimmed, suggested join row inferred from column names (no foreign key); adds that suggested join to the query. Short verb.

add_filter_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: button below the filter rows that adds a new WHERE condition, prefilled with the first available column.

add_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: button below the join list that opens column pickers for defining a join by hand between two tables on the canvas.

add_order_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Order by: button that adds an ORDER BY row for the first selected column, ascending by default.

alias_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Columns: placeholder in the optional input beside each selected column where the user types a column alias (AS name). Single lowercase word.

and_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: placeholder in the second value input of a BETWEEN-style condition, i.e. the upper bound after “and”. Single lowercase word.

cancel_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins → manual join editor: button beside “Add” that discards the join being defined and closes the column pickers.

columns_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the DISTINCT switch and the list of selected output columns.

confirm_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins → manual join editor: button under the from/to column pickers that adds the defined inner join to the query. Short verb.

dialog_title.location: Query Builder dialog → Title bar: title of the visual query builder window, opened from the Tools menu, the command palette, or a table's context menu in the object explorer.

error_disconnected_table.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview when a table on the canvas has no join path to the first table; {alias} is that table's alias.
error_disconnected_table.value: La tabla {alias} no está unida a la primera tabla

error_group_by.location: Query → Query Builder → Validation: error shown when aggregates are selected without grouping every non-aggregate select-list column.
error_group_by.value: Añade a GROUP BY cada columna de la lista de selección que no sea un agregado

error_no_columns.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview when tables are added but no output column is ticked yet; Insert and Run stay disabled.

error_no_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview while the canvas is empty, telling the user to pick a table from the list on the left.
error_no_tables.value: Añade una tabla para comenzar a construir la consulta

filter_tables_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): placeholder in the search box above the list of database tables; typing narrows the list by name.

group_by_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the GROUP BY controls (SQL clause name).

inferred_join_label.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: dim tag at the end of a join row that was guessed from column names rather than a foreign key; {percent} is the model's confidence (0–100).

insert_button.location: Query Builder dialog → footer: button that pastes the formatted SQL from the preview into the active editor tab and closes the dialog; disabled while the query is incomplete.

joins_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading at the top of the panel, above the list of joins between tables.

limit_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the row-limit input (caps how many rows the generated query returns).

limit_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Limit: placeholder in the numeric input where the user types the maximum number of rows to return.

loading_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line with a spinner under the filter box while the connected database's tables are still being loaded and the list is empty; tells the user the dialog is working, not frozen.

no_matching_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line under the filter box when the typed filter matches no table or view name.
no_matching_tables.value: Ninguna tabla coincide con el filtro

no_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line under the filter box when the connected database finished loading and has no tables or views.
no_tables.value: No hay tablas en esta base de datos

order_by_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the ORDER BY rows and the “Add order” button (SQL clause name).

preview_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the live, formatted SQL preview box at the bottom of the panel.

refreshing_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line with a spinner under the filter box while the table list (shown from cache) is being refreshed from the server in the background.

run_button.location: Query Builder dialog → footer: primary button that sends the generated SQL to an editor tab and executes it; disabled while the query is incomplete. Imperative verb.

value_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: placeholder in the first value input of a filter condition, where the user types the value to compare the column against. Single lowercase word.

where_caption.location: Query → Query Builder → Filters: caption above the WHERE condition rows.

aliases_resolved.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: note under the headline giving how many table aliases from the query text were replaced by the real table names; {count} is a number.
aliases_resolved.value: Alias de tabla mostrados como nombres de tabla: {count}

alternatives_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → expanded finding: heading above the list of other fixes that could be tried instead of the main suggestion.

baseline_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: button showing which earlier capture is the baseline; clicking cycles to the next capture. {capture} is a label like “Capture 2 · Estimated plan”.

baseline_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of results when no baseline capture is available to compare from.

bottleneck_tag.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → all views: small outlined tag on the one operator the statement spends the most time (or estimated cost) in. Single noun.

breakdown_by_family.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: heading of the list that totals the plan by kind of work (scans, joins, sorts, aggregates).

breakdown_by_operator.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: heading of the list that totals the plan by operator name.

breakdown_by_table.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: heading of the list that totals the plan by the table each operator reads.

breakdown_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: message shown instead of the chart when the plan carries neither timings nor cost estimates.
breakdown_unavailable.value: Este plan no tiene tiempos ni estimaciones de coste, así que no hay nada que desglosar.

capture_label.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: name of one captured plan inside the Baseline/Comparison buttons; {sequence} is the capture number, {kind} is “Estimated plan” or “Actual plan”.

capture_not_retained.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: warning at the bottom of the pane when a very large plan is shown but not kept for later comparison; {node_count} is its operator count, {limit} the maximum.
capture_not_retained.value: Esta captura tiene {node_count} operadores y no se conservó para la comparación (límite: {limit}).

capture_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: fallback text inside the Baseline or Comparison button when the selected capture no longer exists. Single word.

capturing_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: disabled label of the Re-capture button while a new plan capture is running. Short progress word.

capturing_status.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: centered progress message in the pane body while a plan is being captured; {kind} is the lowercase plan type, “estimated plan” or “actual plan”.

analysis_failed.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: error message in the pane body when the background analysis of a very large plan stopped with an internal error, so no story or findings can be shown.
analysis_failed.value: No se pudo analizar este plan: el análisis se detuvo por un error interno. Abre o captura el plan de nuevo.

analysing_status.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: centered progress message in the pane body while a very large plan is analyzed in the background, before its story and findings appear; {node_count} is the number of operators in the plan.

change_better.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: tag on a change between two captures that made the plan cheaper or faster. Single word.

change_neutral.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: tag on a change between two captures that is neither clearly better nor worse. Single word.

change_worse.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: tag on a change between two captures that made the plan more expensive or slower. Single word.

compare_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button shown once two or more plans were captured; switches the pane to a side-by-side comparison of two captures.

comparison_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: button showing which capture is compared against the baseline; clicking cycles to the next capture. {capture} is a label like “Capture 3 · Actual plan”.

comparison_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of results when no capture is selected to compare against the baseline.

confidence_high.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → expanded finding: how sure the analysis is about this finding, highest level.

confidence_low.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → expanded finding: how sure the analysis is about this finding, lowest level.

confidence_medium.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → expanded finding: how sure the analysis is about this finding, middle level.

copy_finding_sql_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view → finding row: small button that copies the finding's suggested fix SQL to the clipboard; shown only for findings that include SQL.

details_about_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → operator details panel: heading above the plain-language description of what this kind of operator does.

details_findings_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → operator details panel: heading above the findings that concern the selected operator.

details_hint.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → operator details panel: placeholder text while no operator is selected.
details_hint.value: Seleccione un operador para ver qué hizo, cuánto costó y qué informó el motor sobre él.

different_query_context.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of a comparison when the two chosen captures came from different SQL text, so operators cannot be matched up.
different_query_context.value: Estas capturas pertenecen a textos de consulta diferentes y no se pueden alinear de forma segura

distinct_captures_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown when the Baseline and Comparison buttons point at the same capture; the user must pick two different ones.

empty_all_modes.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: empty-state guidance in the pane before any plan is captured, on engines that support both plan types; names the toolbar Explain button and its ⌘L shortcut.
empty_all_modes.value: Explica la consulta actual (botón Explicar o ⌘L) para ver su plan aquí.

empty_estimated_only.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: empty-state guidance before any plan is captured, on engines that only support estimated plans; names the Query menu command “Explain Query (Estimated, No Execution)” and the command palette.
empty_estimated_only.value: Usa Explicar consulta (estimado, sin ejecución) desde el menú Consulta o la paleta de comandos para ver aquí el plan de esta consulta.

estimated_notice.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: note under the headline when the plan was not executed, so every number is an optimizer estimate.
estimated_notice.value: Plan estimado: las filas y los costes son estimaciones del optimizador, no mediciones.

evidence_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → expanded finding: heading above the numbers from the plan that support the finding.

findings_count.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: dim section heading above the list of detected plan problems; {count} is how many findings this statement has.

findings_empty_plan.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: message filling the pane body when the captured plan has no statements to show findings for.
findings_empty_plan.value: El plan no contenía ninguna instrucción.

fit_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: button that zooms and centres the diagram so the whole plan is visible. Single verb.

flame_help.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: one-line explanation under the flame chart of how to read it.
flame_help.value: Cada barra es un operador y su ancho es su parte de la instrucción. Los operadores de los que lee están debajo. Haga clic en una barra para seleccionar el operador.

flame_total_cost.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: line above the flame chart on a plan without timings; {total} is the statement’s estimated cost, {operators} the number of operators.

flame_total_time.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Time/Cost view: line above the flame chart on a measured plan; {total} is the statement’s run time with its unit, {operators} the number of operators.

heat_label.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: label before the buttons that choose which measure (time, cost, rows…) colours the operator cards.

hide_engine_properties.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → operator details panel: button that collapses the raw property list the database engine reported for the operator.

hide_minor_steps.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: button under the story that hides the low-cost steps again.

import_failed_as.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → import error state: headline when a pasted or opened document was recognised as a plan format but could not be parsed; {format} is the format name, e.g. “PostgreSQL EXPLAIN (text)”.
import_failed_as.value: Esto parece {format}, pero no se pudo leer.

import_failed_unknown.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → import error state: headline when a pasted or opened document matches no plan format the importer knows.
import_failed_unknown.value: Este texto no es un formato de plan que SQLly pueda leer.

import_hint_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → import error state: small heading above the instructions for capturing a plan the importer accepts.
import_hint_heading.value: Cómo obtener un plan que se pueda leer

import_line.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → import error state: where in the document reading stopped when only the line is known; {line} is a 1-based line number.

import_position.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → import error state: where in the document reading stopped; {line} and {column} are 1-based numbers.

kind_actual.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: dim label at the left of the header (also used inside capture names) when the plan came from actually running the query, with real row counts.

kind_estimated.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: dim label at the left of the header (also used inside capture names) when the plan is the optimizer's estimate, captured without running the query.

layout_left_to_right_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: button shown while the root is at the top; switches the diagram to draw the root at the left with inputs to the right.

layout_top_down_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: button shown while the root is at the left; switches the diagram to draw the root at the top with inputs below.

learn_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → findings and operator details: heading above links to articles on sqlly.app that explain the operator or problem.

learn_link_tool.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Learn more links: link text for an interactive tool on the sqlly.app website, shown instead of the English page title when the interface is not in English; the page address appears on the line below.

learn_link_snippet.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Learn more links: link text for a ready-made diagnostic SQL query on the sqlly.app website, shown instead of the English page title when the interface is not in English; the page address appears on the line below.

learn_link_setting.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Learn more links: link text for the reference page of one database server setting on the sqlly.app website, shown instead of the English page title when the interface is not in English; the page address appears on the line below.
learn_link_setting.value: Referencia del ajuste del servidor en sqlly.app

learn_link_function.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Learn more links: link text for the reference page of one SQL function on the sqlly.app website, shown instead of the English page title when the interface is not in English; the page address appears on the line below.
learn_link_function.value: Referencia de la función SQL en sqlly.app

learn_link_article.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Learn more links: link text for an article on the sqlly.app website, shown instead of the English article title when the interface is not in English; the page address appears on the line below.

legend_heaviest_path.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → legend: label next to the thick accent line sample that marks the chain of operators where most of the work happens.

legend_high.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → legend: label at the hot end of the colour scale. Lower case, single word.

legend_low.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → legend: label at the cool end of the colour scale. Lower case, single word.

legend_rows.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → legend: label next to thin and thick line samples; connector thickness shows how many rows flow between operators.

mode_cost.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button for the flame chart and breakdown on a plan without timings, where they measure estimated cost. Single noun.

mode_diagram.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button that shows the plan as a graphical diagram of operator boxes. Single noun.

mode_operators.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button that shows every operator as a row of a sortable grid. Single noun.

mode_summary.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button (the default) that shows the step-by-step story of the query beside the ranked findings. Single noun.

mode_time.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button for the flame chart and breakdown on a measured plan, where they show where the time went. Single noun.

never_executed_tag.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → story step: tag on an operator the engine planned but did not run at all.

no_findings.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: reassuring message in place of the findings list when the analysis found no problems in this statement's plan.
no_findings.value: Ninguna de las comprobaciones encontró un problema en este plan.

no_operator_changes.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: message in place of the operator change list when the two captures differ in no meaningful way per operator.
no_operator_changes.value: No se detectaron cambios significativos en los operadores.

no_timing_notice.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: note under the headline when the plan has measured row counts but the engine recorded no time per operator.
no_timing_notice.value: Este plan tiene recuentos de filas medidos, pero no tiempos por operador.

open_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that opens a file picker to load a saved execution plan file from disk into the pane.

open_finding_tab_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view → finding row: small button beside “Copy SQL” that opens the finding's suggested fix SQL in a new editor tab.

paste_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that loads an execution plan (XML or JSON) from the clipboard into the pane.

recapture_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that captures the same kind of plan (estimated or actual) again for the current query; disabled with a tooltip when the engine can't.

schema_used.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: note under the headline when the findings were checked against the table and index definitions already cached for the connection.
schema_used.value: Los hallazgos también usan las definiciones de tablas e índices en caché para esta conexión.

search_matches.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: count of operators matching the search text; {count} is a number.

search_placeholder.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: placeholder in the search box that finds operators by operator name, table or index.

severity_critical.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → findings: severity word shown beside the severity icon of the most serious findings, so colour is not the only signal. Single word.

severity_info.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → findings: severity word shown beside the severity icon of informational findings, so colour is not the only signal. Single word.

severity_warning.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → findings: severity word shown beside the severity icon of findings worth fixing, so colour is not the only signal. Single word.

show_engine_properties.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → operator details panel: button that expands the raw property list the database engine reported for the operator.

show_in_diagram_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → findings and story steps: button that switches to the Diagram view with this operator selected and scrolled into view.

show_minor_steps.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: button under the story that reveals the low-cost steps left out by default; {count} is how many are hidden.

show_plan_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: label of the Compare toggle while the comparison view is open; clicking returns to the normal single-plan view.

statement_fallback.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header → statement switcher: generic word used in a statement tab in place of the statement type when the plan does not name one.

statement_tab.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header → statement switcher: tab for one statement of a multi-statement batch; {number} is its position, {statement_type} its kind (e.g. SELECT).

step_inputs.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view → story step: small line naming the earlier steps this step reads its rows from; {steps} is a comma-separated list of step numbers.

story_heading.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Summary view: heading above the numbered list of steps that tells what the query does in execution order.
story_heading.value: Qué hace la consulta, en orden

table_header_factor.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Operators view → grid: column header for the estimate-error column, whose cells are bare multipliers; {label} is the column name.

table_header_kb.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Operators view → grid: column header for the memory column, whose cells are bare numbers of kilobytes; {label} is the column name.

table_header_ms.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Operators view → grid: column header for the time columns, whose cells are bare numbers of milliseconds; {label} is the column name.

zoom_in_tooltip.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: tooltip of the “+” button that enlarges the diagram.

zoom_out_tooltip.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view → toolbar: tooltip of the “−” button that shrinks the diagram.

disconnected.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover (chevron beside the Explain button): message filling the popover when no connection is active, so plan options can't be set.
disconnected.value: Conéctate para configurar las opciones de EXPLAIN

flag_analyze.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags: checkbox label for PostgreSQL/MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE; warns that the statement is actually executed to get real timings.

flag_buffers.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the BUFFERS option, adding shared/local buffer usage to the plan. Usually left as the technical term.

flag_costs.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the COSTS option, showing the optimizer's estimated startup and total cost per operator.

flag_generic_plan.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 16+): checkbox label for the GENERIC_PLAN option, planning a parameterized query without specific parameter values.

flag_memory.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 17+): checkbox label for the MEMORY option, reporting the planner's memory use.

flag_settings.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 12+): checkbox label for the SETTINGS option, listing non-default planner configuration settings in the plan (not the app's settings).

flag_summary.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the SUMMARY option, adding planning and execution time totals after the plan.

flag_timing.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the TIMING option, recording actual time per operator when Analyze is on.

flag_unknown.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags: generic fallback checkbox label for an EXPLAIN option the app has no name for. Single noun.

flag_verbose.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the VERBOSE option, adding output column lists and schema-qualified names to the plan.

flag_wal.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 13+): checkbox label for the WAL option, reporting write-ahead-log records generated. Acronym; usually kept as is.

preset_actual.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that captures an actual plan by running the query with the selected options. Short adjective; sits beside “Estimated” and “Profile”.

preset_estimated.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that captures an estimated plan without executing the query. Short adjective; sits beside “Actual” and “Profile”.

preset_profile.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that runs and profiles the query to capture an actual plan, allowed only for read-only SELECT statements.

reset_defaults_button.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: small text button at the bottom of the popover that restores every EXPLAIN option checkbox to its default state.

version_known.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover naming the connected server; {product} is the engine (e.g. PostgreSQL), {major}.{minor} its version, which decides available flags.

version_probing.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover while the app is still asking the server for its version, before flag availability is known.

version_unknown.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover when the server version could not be determined; flags assume a default version.

invalid_pins_file.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippets → Import: error in the status bar when the chosen file is not valid pinned-snippets JSON; {error} is the parser's technical reason.
invalid_pins_file.value: No es un archivo válido de fragmentos fijados: {error}

age_days.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–6 days ago, abbreviated (“d” = days); {count} is the number of days. Must stay very short; older entries show a plain date.

age_hours.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–23 hours ago, abbreviated (“h” = hours); {count} is the number of hours. Must stay very short, sits among other “·”-separated details.

age_just_now.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age shown for an entry run less than a minute ago, between the server/database and the outcome. Lowercase fragment, very short.

age_minutes.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–59 minutes ago, abbreviated (“m” = minutes); {count} is the number of minutes. Must stay very short.

analyze_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that sends the selected history entry (SQL, timing, outcome) to the AI panel for analysis and closes the dialog; disabled when nothing is selected.

analyze_recent_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that sends the first five entries currently visible in the Recent section (after filtering) to the AI panel as one analysis request, then closes the dialog.
analyze_recent_button.value: Analizar las últimas 5 visibles con IA

analyze_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Analyze with AI” in the Query History dialog is triggered with no history entry selected, asking the user to pick an entry first.
analyze_requires_selection.value: Selecciona primero una entrada del historial

copy_rollback_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that copies the rollback (undo) SQL recorded for the selected data-changing entry to the clipboard; enabled only when the entry has rollback SQL.

description_label.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: label in front of the free-text description input, shown only when the selected entry is pinned.

description_placeholder.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: placeholder in the description input for a selected pinned entry, inviting an optional note on what the query is for.

dialog_title.location: Query History dialog → Title bar: title of the modal dialog that lists previously run statements and pinned snippets, opened from the Query History command.

empty_history.location: Query History dialog → Entry list: empty-state message shown when no statements have ever been logged and nothing is pinned, explaining that statements you run will appear here.
empty_history.value: Aún no hay historial de consultas: las instrucciones que ejecutes se registrarán aquí.

empty_search.location: Query History dialog → Entry list: empty-state message shown when history exists but the text typed in the search/filter box matches no pinned or recent entry.
empty_search.value: Ninguna entrada coincide con la búsqueda.

export_library_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that writes every pinned snippet as a .sql file into the “Pinned” folder of the SQL Library (desktop only). “Pins” = pinned snippets, “Library” = the SQL Library.

export_pins_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that opens a save dialog to export all pinned snippets to a JSON file (also usable as a backup); the ellipsis signals a file picker follows.

filter_placeholder.location: Query History dialog → Search box placeholder: placeholder in the search box above the list; free text searches SQL, server and database, and the “key:value” tokens are filter syntax examples that must stay untranslated (server:, db:, outcome:failed, min:1s).
filter_placeholder.value: Buscar o filtrar: server:prod db:sales outcome:failed min:1s

footer.location: Query History dialog → Footer: small status line under the list with counts ({pinned_count} pinned entries shown, {recent_count} recent entries shown, {removed_count} entries dropped by the retention limit), the filter key names (keep untranslated) and a tip on opening an entry.
footer.value: {pinned_count} fijadas · {recent_count} recientes · {removed_count} eliminadas por retención · filtros: server/db/outcome/after/before/min/max/tag · haz doble clic o usa Abrir en nueva pestaña para insertar la instrucción completa en una pestaña del editor

import_file_filter.location: Query History dialog → Import Pins file picker: name of the file-type filter (JSON files) in the system open dialog that appears after clicking “Import Pins…”.

import_pins_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that opens a file picker to import pinned snippets from a previously exported JSON file, merging them and skipping ones already pinned (desktop only).

import_read_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown after “Import Pins…” in the Query History dialog when the chosen file cannot be read; {path} is the file path, {error} the operating-system error text.

library_export_partial.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown after “Export Pins to Library” in the Query History dialog when only some snippet files could be written; {written} succeeded out of {total}, {error} is the last write error.

library_exported.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after “Export Pins to Library” in the Query History dialog wrote every pinned snippet as a .sql file; {count} is the number of files written to the SQL Library “Pinned” folder.
library_exported.value: Se exportaron {count} consultas fijadas a la biblioteca

library_folder_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown after “Export Pins to Library” in the Query History dialog when the “Pinned” folder inside the SQL Library cannot be created; {error} is the operating-system error text.
library_folder_failed.value: No se pudo crear la carpeta de la biblioteca: {error}

load_more.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Bottom of Recent section: clickable link that loads the next page of entries; {remaining} is how many further matches exist, {more_suffix} is “+” when the on-disk log may hold even more, otherwise empty.

load_more_from_log.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Bottom of Recent section: alternative wording of the load-more link used when the count of further matches is unknown, reading older entries from the history log file.

name_label.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: label in front of the name input, shown only when the selected entry is pinned; a named pin is listed by this name as a saved query.

name_placeholder.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: placeholder in the name input for a selected pinned entry; the name becomes the row title in place of the SQL preview.

no_pins_for_library_export.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Export Pins to Library” in the Query History dialog is clicked but nothing is pinned, so no .sql files are written to the SQL Library.
no_pins_for_library_export.value: No hay fragmentos fijados para exportar

no_pins_to_export.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Export Pins…” (JSON file export) in the Query History dialog is clicked but nothing is pinned, so no save dialog opens.
no_pins_to_export.value: No hay fragmentos fijados para exportar

no_recent_to_analyze.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Analyze last 5 visible with AI” in the Query History dialog finds no entries in the Recent section (e.g. the filter hides them all).
no_recent_to_analyze.value: No hay entradas recientes para analizar

no_rollback_sql.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Copy rollback SQL” in the Query History dialog is triggered for a selected entry that has no recorded rollback (undo) statement.
no_rollback_sql.value: Esta entrada no tiene SQL de reversión

open_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that copies the full SQL of the selected entry into a new editor tab without running it and closes the dialog; same as double-click or Enter on a row.

open_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Open in New Tab” (or Enter) in the Query History dialog is used with no history entry selected.
open_requires_selection.value: Selecciona primero una entrada del historial

outcome_cancelled.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix appended after the age when the statement was cancelled by the user; starts with a space and a “·” separator that must be kept.

outcome_failed.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix appended after the age when the statement ended with an error; starts with a space and a “·” separator that must be kept.

outcome_succeeded.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix appended after the age when the statement completed successfully; starts with a space and a “·” separator that must be kept.

pin_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: toggle button that pins the selected entry as a keeper snippet, moving it into the Pinned section; switches to “Unpin” when the selection is already pinned.

pin_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when the Pin/Unpin button in the Query History dialog is triggered with no history entry selected.
pin_requires_selection.value: Selecciona primero una entrada del historial

pinned_badge.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Recent row detail line: suffix marking a recent entry whose statement is also pinned; starts with a space and a “·” separator that must be kept.

pinned_section.location: Query History dialog → Entry list: small section heading above the pinned snippets, shown first in the list when at least one pinned entry matches the filter.

pins_export_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when writing the JSON file chosen in the “Export Pins…” save dialog of the Query History dialog fails; {error} is the operating-system error text.
pins_export_failed.value: No se pudieron exportar los fragmentos fijados: {error}

pins_exported.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after “Export Pins…” in the Query History dialog saved the JSON file; {count} is the number of pinned snippets exported, {path} the saved file path.

pins_imported.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after “Import Pins…” in the Query History dialog merged a JSON file; {count} is the number of newly added pinned snippets (duplicates are skipped).

provenance_ai.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix marking a statement that was generated and run by the AI assistant; starts with a space and a “·” separator. Keep “AI” short.

provenance_tool.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix marking a statement run by a built-in tool (e.g. an admin dialog) rather than typed by the user; starts with a space and a “·” separator.

recent_section.location: Query History dialog → Entry list: small section heading above the recently run statements from the execution log, shown below the Pinned section.

rollback_copied.location: Workbench → Status bar: success message after “Copy rollback SQL” in the Query History dialog put the selected entry's undo statement on the clipboard.
rollback_copied.value: SQL de reversión copiado al portapapeles

rollback_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Copy rollback SQL” in the Query History dialog is triggered with no history entry selected.
rollback_requires_selection.value: Selecciona primero una entrada del historial

rows_affected.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: suffix giving how many rows a data-changing statement affected; {count} is the row count; starts with a space and a “·” separator that must be kept.

run_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that opens the selected entry's SQL in a new editor tab and executes it immediately, then closes the dialog. Imperative verb.

run_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when the Run button in the Query History dialog is triggered with no history entry selected.
run_requires_selection.value: Selecciona primero una entrada del historial

tags_label.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: label in front of the tags input, shown only when the selected entry is pinned; tags appear as #tag in the row and can be filtered with tag:.

tags_placeholder.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: placeholder in the tags input for a selected pinned entry, telling the user to separate several tags with commas.
tags_placeholder.value: Etiquetas para el fragmento fijado, separadas por comas

unpin_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: label of the Pin toggle button when the selected entry is already pinned; clicking removes it from the Pinned section.

compare_button.location: Query tab → History side panel → Footer: button that compares the selected saved version with the current editor text and shows the line differences; dimmed until a version is selected.

current_badge.location: Query tab → History side panel → Version timeline: lowercase marker at the end of the row for the version currently loaded in the editor. Very short.

delete_button.location: Query tab → History side panel → Footer: quiet button that deletes the selected saved version from the tab's version history; dimmed until a version is selected.

empty_timeline.location: Query tab → History side panel: empty-state message in the timeline area when the tab has no saved versions yet, explaining that versions are saved when you run the query or pause typing, and that F5 runs it.
empty_timeline.value: Aún no hay versiones. Se guarda una versión al ejecutar la consulta o al pausar la edición; ejecuta con F5 para crear la primera.

file_backed_badge.location: Query tab → History side panel → Footer, right side: small label shown when the query tab is backed by a file on disk (version history survives closing the tab and git history is listed).

git_section.location: Query tab → History side panel → Bottom section: uppercase section heading above the list of git commits touching the tab's file, shown only for file-backed tabs inside a git repository.

no_results.location: Query tab → History side panel → Version timeline row: lowercase note on a run version when result storage is on but no results were saved for that run.

no_versions.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: lowercase subtitle under the panel title when the tab has no saved versions.

restore_button.location: Query tab → History side panel → Footer: primary button that loads the selected saved version back into the editor (same as double-clicking a row); dimmed until a version is selected.

row_count_many.location: Query tab → History side panel → Version timeline row: plural note on a run version giving how many result rows were stored for that run; {count} is the row count (0 or 2+).

row_count_one.location: Query tab → History side panel → Version timeline row: singular note on a run version whose stored result has exactly one row; {count} is 1.

title.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: title of the right-hand side panel that lists the query tab's saved versions (version history), beside the ✕ close button.

version_many.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: plural subtitle giving the number of saved versions when result storage is off; {count} is the number of versions (2+).

version_many_results.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: plural subtitle giving the number of saved versions plus a note that result storage is on (run results are kept with versions); {count} is 2+.

version_one.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: singular subtitle when the tab has exactly one saved version and result storage is off; {count} is 1.

version_one_results.location: Query tab → History side panel → Header: singular subtitle when the tab has exactly one saved version and result storage is on (results are kept with versions); {count} is 1.

opened_many.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after an app using SQLly Embedded launched SQLly and opened several query tabs without a connection; {count} is the number of tabs. Nothing has run yet, the user should review first.
opened_many.value: Se abrieron {count} consultas desde tu aplicación; revísalas antes de ejecutarlas.

opened_many_connected.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after an app using SQLly Embedded launched SQLly, connected, and opened several query tabs on that connection; {count} is the number of tabs (connection not named). Nothing has run yet.
opened_many_connected.value: Se abrieron {count} consultas desde tu aplicación; revísalas antes de ejecutarlas.

opened_one.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after an app using SQLly Embedded launched SQLly and opened a single query tab without a connection. Nothing has run yet; the user should review it first.
opened_one.value: Se abrió una consulta desde tu aplicación; revísala antes de ejecutarla.

opened_one_connected.location: Workbench → Status bar: message after an app using SQLly Embedded launched SQLly and opened one query tab on a connection; {connection} is the connection name. Nothing has run yet.
opened_one_connected.value: Se abrió una consulta en {connection} desde tu aplicación; revísala antes de ejecutarla.

clear_group_button.location: Run on… dialog → Environment group header: small button that unticks every connection in this group; shown in place of “Select all” when all of the group's connections are ticked.

dialog_title.location: Run on… dialog → Title bar: title of the dialog where the user ticks several saved connections to run the current statement against each one. The ellipsis is part of the title.

production_detail.location: Run on… dialog → Connection row: detail line for a connection tagged as Production; {detail} is the server/database summary, followed by a production warning word.

run_many.location: Run on… dialog → Footer: primary button label when zero or several connections are ticked; {count} is the number of selected connections (disabled at 0).

run_one.location: Run on… dialog → Footer: primary button label when exactly one connection is ticked; runs the current statement on that one connection.

select_group_button.location: Run on… dialog → Environment group header: small button that ticks every connection in this environment group (e.g. all Production connections).

subtitle.location: Run on… dialog → Subtitle: explanatory subtitle under the title stating that the current statement runs once on each ticked connection.
subtitle.value: Ejecuta la instrucción actual una vez por cada conexión seleccionada.

equals_required.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” underline message when a “-- sqlly set” line has no “=” between the variable name and its value.
equals_required.value: se requiere = entre el nombre y el valor

invalid_default.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “param directive is ignored” underline message when a “-- sqlly param:” default value does not fit the declared type; {error} is the type error.
invalid_default.value: el valor predeterminado no es válido: {error}

missing_value_many.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Run is pressed but several declared query parameters have neither a typed value nor a default; {names} is a comma-separated list of @names. The first one is focused.

missing_value_one.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Run is pressed but one declared query parameter has neither a typed value nor a default; {names} is that single @name, which is then focused in the Parameters strip.

name_requires_at.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “param directive is ignored” underline message when a “-- sqlly param:” line does not start with an @name or :name. Lowercase fragment.
name_requires_at.value: el nombre del parámetro debe comenzar con @ o :

named_value_invalid.location: Workbench → Status bar: error shown when Run is pressed and a query parameter value fails validation; {name} is the @parameter name and {error} the type error (e.g. “not a valid date”).

type_required.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “param directive is ignored” underline message when a “-- sqlly param: @name” line has no type after the name. Lowercase fragment.
type_required.value: se requiere un tipo después del nombre

value_required.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” underline message when a “-- sqlly set name =” line has nothing after the equals sign. Lowercase fragment.

value_type_invalid.location: Query tab → Parameters strip and Run errors: validation reason shown beside a parameter input (or inside other errors) when the value does not parse as the declared type; {parameter_type} is an untranslated type name such as date, int, uuid.

variable_characters_invalid.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” message when a “-- sqlly set” variable name has characters other than letters, digits or underscores.
variable_characters_invalid.value: el nombre de variable contiene caracteres no válidos

variable_name_required.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” message when a “-- sqlly set” line has nothing before the “=”. Lowercase fragment.
variable_name_required.value: se requiere un nombre de variable

variable_sigil_forbidden.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” message when a “-- sqlly set” variable name begins with @, $ or : (variables are declared without a prefix symbol).
variable_sigil_forbidden.value: los nombres de variable no deben comenzar con @, $ ni :

variable_start_invalid.location: SQL editor → Directive diagnostics: reason inserted into the “set directive is ignored” message when a “-- sqlly set” variable name begins with a digit or other character instead of a letter or underscore.
variable_start_invalid.value: el nombre de variable debe comenzar con una letra o un guion bajo

default_status.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → Parameter row: dim status beside an empty input saying the declared default will be used; {value} is that default value.

generate_uuid_button.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → uuid parameter row: small button beside the input that fills it with a freshly generated random UUID.

generate_uuid_tooltip.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → uuid parameter row: tooltip on the “Generate UUID” button explaining it inserts a new random UUID into the input.

header.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: header line of the band of parameter inputs above the results, explaining values are inserted as safely escaped literals when the query runs.
header.value: Parámetros — se sustituyen tal como se escriben, como literales con escape al ejecutar

placeholder_binary.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a binary parameter, showing hex notation and that NULL is allowed; keep the hex sample as is.

placeholder_bool.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a bool parameter, showing that true or false (or NULL) is expected; keep “true”, “false”, “NULL” untranslated.

placeholder_date.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a date parameter, showing the expected year-month-day format and that NULL is allowed.

placeholder_datetime.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a datetime parameter, showing the expected date and time-of-day format and that NULL is allowed.

placeholder_json.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a json parameter, showing a sample JSON object and that NULL is allowed; keep the JSON sample syntax intact.

placeholder_time.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: placeholder in the input of a time parameter, showing the expected hours:minutes:seconds format and that NULL is allowed.

placeholder_value.location: Query tab → Parameters strip: generic placeholder in the input of a text, number or decimal parameter, saying to type a value or NULL.

placeholder_auto.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → Parameter row: placeholder text inside the input of a :name or ? placeholder found in the SQL, hinting at how the value is read.

auto_type_tooltip.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → Parameter row: tooltip over the “auto” type label of a placeholder found in the SQL without a -- sqlly param: declaration.
auto_type_tooltip.value: Encontrado en el SQL. Los números, true/false y NULL se usan tal cual; todo lo demás se pone entre comillas como texto. Declara -- sqlly param: :name int (o date, text, …) para fijar el tipo.

required_status.location: Query tab → Parameters strip → Parameter row: red status beside an input that is empty and has no declared default, meaning a value must be entered before Run.

summary.location: Run Statements dialog → Checklist summary line (reads only): summary line under the statement checklist when only read statements are ticked; {selected} is the ticked count, {total} the number of statements in the script.
summary.value: {selected} de {total} instrucciones

summary_updates.location: Run Statements dialog → Checklist summary line (with UPDATEs): summary line under the checklist when ticked statements include UPDATEs; {selected} ticked of {total}, {update_count} is how many are UPDATE (keep UPDATE as the SQL keyword).

summary_writes.location: Run Statements dialog → Checklist summary line (with writes): summary line when ticked statements include writes but no UPDATE; {selected} ticked of {total}, {write_count} is how many statements modify data or schema.

issue_count_many.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL result: plural count of findings inserted into the validation summary; {count} is the number of issues (2+, or 0 in some cases).

issue_count_one.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL result: singular count inserted into the validation summary when the SQL has exactly one finding.

severity_confirmation.location: AI panel → Generated SQL review: severity label before an issue that needs explicit confirmation, such as UPDATE or DELETE without a WHERE clause affecting a whole table.

severity_error.location: AI panel → Generated SQL review: severity label before an issue that blocks running the generated SQL (e.g. a parse error or unknown object). Noun, followed by a colon and the message.

severity_info.location: AI panel → Generated SQL review: severity label before a purely informational note about the generated SQL. Short noun, followed by a colon and the message.

severity_warning.location: AI panel → Generated SQL review: severity label before a non-blocking warning about the generated SQL. Noun, followed by a colon and the message.

summary_confirmation.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL result: summary when the SQL contains an operation needing confirmation (e.g. no WHERE clause); {issue_count} is the already-formatted issue count such as “2 issues”.

summary_ok.location: Workbench → Status bar → Validate SQL result: summary inserted after “Validation summary:” when the SQL validated with no issues at all.

checking.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: dim progress message shown while the dialog checks whether the server’s statistics source is enabled; {source} is the source name, e.g. “SQL Server Query Store”.

cumulative_since_reset.location: Query Insights dialog → Footer buttons: disabled time-window button label for engines whose statistics cannot be filtered by time (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle); means figures accumulate since the statistics were last reset.

cumulative_statistics.location: Query Insights dialog → Footer caption: lowercase phrase filling the {window} slot of the top-queries caption when the engine has no time window, e.g. “…by avg duration (cumulative statistics)”.

current_database.location: Query Insights dialog → Subtitle: lowercase fallback filling the {database} slot when the connection has no default database selected (non–SQL Server engines); refers to whichever database the session is using.

dialog_title.location: Query Insights dialog → Title bar: title bar of the dialog (and of its popped-out window) listing the most expensive or most frequent queries recorded by the server; opened from the Tools menu, Object Explorer, or Command Palette.

disabled_clickhouse.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: explanation shown on ClickHouse connections when query logging is off or the system query_log table does not exist yet; keep setting names and SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS untranslated.
disabled_clickhouse.value: El registro de consultas está desactivado para este usuario (log_queries = 0) o system.query_log aún no se ha creado, por lo que ClickHouse no tiene historial de consultas para mostrar. Configura log_queries = 1 en users.xml o en el perfil de configuración del usuario, ejecuta una consulta y luego SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS.

disabled_mysql.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: explanation shown on MySQL/MariaDB connections when Performance Schema is turned off on the server, so no statement statistics can be read.
disabled_mysql.value: Performance Schema está deshabilitado en este servidor. Habilítalo en la configuración del servidor y reinicia MySQL/MariaDB para que Información de consultas pueda leer los resúmenes de instrucciones.

disabled_oracle.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: explanation shown on Oracle connections when the shared pool (V$SQLAREA) contains no executed statements yet, so there are no statistics to list.
disabled_oracle.value: El pool compartido aún no contiene cursores ejecutados, por lo que no hay estadísticas de instrucciones para mostrar.

disabled_postgres.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: explanation shown on PostgreSQL connections when the pg_stat_statements extension is not installed in the database; the button below can script its CREATE EXTENSION statement.
disabled_postgres.value: pg_stat_statements no está instalado en esta base de datos, por lo que PostgreSQL no tiene estadísticas acumuladas de instrucciones para mostrar aquí.

disabled_sqlserver.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: explanation shown on SQL Server when Query Store is turned off for the database; {database} is the database name in square brackets. A button below scripts the enable statement.
disabled_sqlserver.value: Query Store está desactivado para [{database}], por lo que no hay historial de consultas capturado para mostrar.

empty.location: Query Insights dialog → Results area: dim message shown when the statistics source is enabled but returned no rows; {source} is the source name, e.g. “PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements”.
empty.value: {source} está disponible, pero no ha capturado ninguna consulta todavía.

failures_footer.location: Query Insights dialog → Footer caption (ClickHouse, failures view): describes the list; {limit} is the row cap (50), {source} the source name, {window} the lowercase time window, e.g. “last hour”. Names the Open Selected Query button.
failures_footer.value: Las {limit} consultas fallidas más recientes de {source} ({window}) · selecciona una fila y usa Abrir consulta seleccionada para editarla en una pestaña

guidance_clickhouse.location: Query Insights dialog → Error message: second paragraph appended after the error when the ClickHouse query log could not be read; explains the server settings and permissions required. Keep setting names untranslated.
guidance_clickhouse.value: Información de consultas de ClickHouse lee system.query_log, que requiere log_queries = 1 para el usuario conectado (users.xml o un perfil de configuración), la tabla query_log habilitada en config.xml y permiso para leer la base de datos system. El servidor escribe el registro cada pocos segundos; ejecuta SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS para ver las consultas más recientes de inmediato.

guidance_mysql.location: Query Insights dialog → Error message: second paragraph appended after the error when MySQL/MariaDB statement digests could not be read; explains the Performance Schema setup and permissions needed.
guidance_mysql.value: Información de consultas de MySQL/MariaDB requiere consumidores de resúmenes de instrucciones de Performance Schema y permiso para leer performance_schema; habilitar Performance Schema puede requerir configuración del servidor y un reinicio.

guidance_oracle.location: Query Insights dialog → Error message: second paragraph appended after the error when Oracle’s V$SQLAREA could not be read; tells the user which grant to request from a DBA. Keep view and role names untranslated.
guidance_oracle.value: Información de consultas de Oracle lee el pool compartido mediante V$SQLAREA; pide a un DBA permiso SELECT sobre V_$SQLAREA (o SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE) para este inicio de sesión.
