feedback_full_model_help.location: Settings → Editor → General → IntelliSense: help text under the “Include full data model…” checkbox clarifying it pre-ticks “Include all” in that dialog and that only object names, never data, are sent.
feedback_full_model_help.value: Preselecciona «Incluir todo» en el diálogo Mejorar IntelliSense: solo nombres de objetos, nunca datos.

fiscal_year_help.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: help text under the “Fiscal year starts in” dropdown listing affected phrases and explaining a fiscal year is named for the calendar year it ends in.
fiscal_year_help.value: Para this fiscal year, last fiscal year y fytd. Un año fiscal recibe el nombre del año natural en el que termina.

highlight_occurrences_help.location: Settings → Editor → General → Selection: help text under the “Highlight occurrences of selection” checkbox describing the VS Code–style highlight and noting it never changes the text.
highlight_occurrences_help.value: Al seleccionar una palabra o frase, se resaltan suavemente los demás lugares en los que aparece en el script, como hace VS Code, para que los nombres y valores repetidos se vean de un vistazo. El resaltado sigue la selección y nunca cambia el texto.

detect_query_placeholders_help.location: Settings → Editor → General → Query parameters: help text under the placeholder checkbox explaining that values are entered in the Parameters strip and how they are read.
detect_query_placeholders_help.value: Un marcador como WHERE id = :id obtiene un campo en la franja de parámetros sobre los resultados, y Ejecutar usa lo que escribas sin modificar tu script. Los números, true/false y NULL se interpretan como tales; todo lo demás es texto, y las comillas ('42') fuerzan texto. En SQL Server, un @name que el script nunca declara con DECLARE funciona igual. Se ignoran los marcadores dentro de cadenas y comentarios.

period_ranges_help.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: help text under “Turn periods into ranges” explaining how each comparison operator uses the period's first or last moment; operators stay unchanged.
period_ranges_help.value: Con =, today, november o last week se convierte en un intervalo que cubre todo el período; con <>, el intervalo se excluye. > y <= comparan con el último instante del período; >= y <, con el primero. Si está desactivado, un período significa su primer instante.

plain_dates_help.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: help text under the plain-words checkbox explaining how to trigger it with Ctrl+Shift+Space after a date comparison; example words and column names stay unchanged.
plain_dates_help.value: Tras una comparación de fechas como OrderDate = o created_at >=, presiona Ctrl+Shift+Space y escribe today, last wed at 3, november, ytd o past 7 days. La tarjeta muestra su significado; Enter escribe la fecha correspondiente. En cualquier otro lugar, el atajo sigue buscando valores de columnas.

range_style_help.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: help text under the Range style dropdown comparing the BETWEEN form with the half-open form; SQL keywords and the time value stay unchanged.
range_style_help.value: BETWEEN resulta natural y termina en el último instante que la columna puede almacenar (23:59:59.997 para datetime de SQL Server). La forma de intervalo semiabierto es exacta para cualquier precisión, pero escribe el nombre de la columna dos veces.

restore_tabs_help.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → Restore tabs at launch: help text under the restore options clarifying all tabs stay saved in the workspace file and the choice only affects what reopens.
restore_tabs_help.value: El archivo del espacio de trabajo siempre conserva todas las pestañas; esto solo controla cuáles se vuelven a abrir.

schema_name_search.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Matching: help text under the “Include schema name in searching” checkbox with examples of the on and off behavior; example names stay unchanged.
schema_name_search.value: dboM o dbom encuentra dbo.Make. Si está desactivado, solo se busca por el nombre del objeto, salvo que escribas el esquema y un punto (dbo.m).

source_help.location: Settings → Editor → General → IntelliSense: help text under the Source dropdown explaining the difference between the Built-in and Rust engine options.
source_help.value: Integrado usa el analizador local; Motor Rust ejecuta el analizador más completo, basado en FFI.

terminal_editor_note.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: help text shown at the bottom of the pane when the selected editor is a terminal program (such as nano or vi), saying it will open in a new Terminal window.
terminal_editor_note.value: Es un editor de terminal; se abre en una nueva ventana de Terminal.

to_date_range_end.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: help text under the “To-date periods end” dropdown listing which phrases it affects; ytd and mtd are typed abbreviations and stay unchanged.
to_date_range_end.value: Para ytd, mtd, this year so far, past 7 days y expresiones similares.

vim_mode_keys.location: Settings → Editor → General → Display: help text under the Vim keybindings checkbox listing the supported Vim keys and motions; key letters and symbols must stay unchanged.
vim_mode_keys.value: Esc entra en modo Normal; i / a / o entran en modo Insertar. Movimientos h j k l w b e 0 $ gg G, operadores d c y con dd / yy / cc, x, p / P, u y Ctrl+R, v para Visual y / para abrir Buscar.

external_editors_intro.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: introductory sentence under the pane heading saying the chosen editor opens JSON / XML values from the results grid.
external_editors_intro.value: Elige el editor predeterminado para abrir valores de datos estructurados (JSON / XML) desde la cuadrícula de resultados.

feedback_kinds_intro.location: Settings → Editor → General → Feedback report object kinds: explanatory paragraph under the section heading; notes the choice can be changed per report and that picking a table always includes its columns and foreign keys.
feedback_kinds_intro.value: Qué tipos de objetos muestra de forma predeterminada el diálogo Mejorar IntelliSense. Se puede ajustar en cada informe; al elegir una tabla siempre se incluyen todas sus columnas y claves foráneas.

general_intro.location: Settings → Editor → General: introductory sentence under the pane heading summarizing what the pane controls (line numbers, bold text, indentation).
general_intro.value: Configura el comportamiento básico del editor: números de línea, texto en negrita e indentación.

intellisense_intro.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense: introductory sentences under the pane heading saying the settings govern suggestion matching and insertion in every query tab.
intellisense_intro.value: Cómo se buscan e insertan las sugerencias de autocompletado. Estos ajustes se aplican a todas las pestañas de consulta.

tabs_intro.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs: introductory sentence under the pane heading summarizing the launch-restore and disconnect options below.
tabs_intro.value: Elige qué pestañas se recuperan al iniciar y qué ocurre con ellas al desconectarte.

comma_placement.location: Settings → Editor → General → Automagic commas: label beside the Trailing / Leading radio pair choosing where automatically inserted commas go.

date_periods_end.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the dropdown choosing where to-date periods (ytd, mtd, past 7 days) stop: end of today or the current moment.
date_periods_end.value: Fin de los períodos hasta la fecha

day_month_its_own.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the dropdown deciding which occurrence a bare weekday or month name (e.g. “wed”, “november”) refers to.
day_month_its_own.value: Un día o mes por sí solo

fiscal_year_starts.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the month dropdown choosing the month a fiscal year begins in.

range_style.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the dropdown choosing how a date range is written in SQL (BETWEEN … AND … or a >= … AND < … pair).

source.location: Settings → Editor → General → IntelliSense: label beside the dropdown that picks the completion engine (Built-in or Rust engine) used for suggestions.

spaces_per_tab.location: Settings → Editor → General → Indentation: label beside a − / + number stepper setting how many spaces one indent level (one press of Tab) is worth.

time_without_am_pm.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the dropdown deciding how an hour typed without am or pm (e.g. “at 3”) is read.

weeks_start.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: label beside the Sunday / Monday dropdown choosing the first day of the week for phrases like “this week” or “last week”.

reset_default.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors → Binary path: button under the path field that discards a custom path and restores the chosen editor's standard install path; shown for listed editors, not Other.

april.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option April.

august.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option August.

december.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option December.

february.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option February.

january.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option January.

july.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option July.

june.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option June.

march.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option March.

may.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option May.

november.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option November.

october.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option October.

september.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Fiscal year starts: month option September.

at_end_today.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → To-date periods end: dropdown option making ytd/mtd-style ranges run through the end of the current day.
at_end_today.value: Al final del día de hoy

bare_hour_24h.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → A time without am/pm: dropdown option reading bare hours on a 24-hour clock; the example shows “at 3” becoming 3:00 AM.
bare_hour_24h.value: Formato de 24 horas (a las 3 = 3:00 a. m.)

bare_hour_business.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → A time without am/pm: dropdown option reading hours 1 to 7 as afternoon (business hours); the example in parentheses shows “at 3” becoming 3:00 PM.
bare_hour_business.value: De 1 a 7 es por la tarde (a las 3 = 3:00 p. m.)

means_most_recent_one.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → A day or month on its own: dropdown option meaning a bare weekday or month refers to the most recent past one.

means_next_one.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → A day or month on its own: dropdown option meaning a bare weekday or month refers to the next upcoming one.

means_week_s_year_s.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → A day or month on its own: dropdown option meaning a bare weekday is the one in the current week and a bare month the one in the current year.
means_week_s_year_s.value: Significa el de esta semana / el de este año

monday.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Weeks start on: dropdown option making weeks begin on Monday.

right_now.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → To-date periods end: dropdown option making ytd/mtd-style ranges stop at the current moment.

sunday.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience → Weeks start on: dropdown option making weeks begin on Sunday.

alias_from_capitals.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Alias names: radio option that builds the alias from the table name's capital letters in lower case; the example in parentheses stays unchanged.

alias_on_second_accept.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → When you accept a table or view: radio option that instead offers the alias as a follow-up suggestion, added only when Enter or Tab is pressed again.
alias_on_second_accept.value: Ofrecer el alias como segunda sugerencia (vuelve a presionar Enter o Tab para añadirlo)

all_tabs.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → Restore tabs at launch: radio option that reopens every query tab from the last session when SQLLY starts.

auto_add_alias.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → When you accept a table or view: radio option that inserts the generated alias right after the table name immediately; example stays unchanged.
auto_add_alias.value: Añadir el alias automáticamente (Orders AS o)

auto_based_join.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Alias names: radio option that picks the alias automatically depending on the join being written.

close_tabs.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → When disconnecting: radio option that closes the disconnected connection's query tabs, except pinned tabs and tabs with unsaved changes.
close_tabs.value: Cerrar las pestañas de la conexión (se conservan las pestañas fijadas y las no guardadas)

disconnect_clear_results.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → When disconnecting: radio option that keeps the connection's query tabs open but empties their results panes.
disconnect_clear_results.value: Mantener las pestañas pero borrar sus resultados

do_not_suggest.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Alias names: radio option that turns table alias suggestions off entirely.

keep_tabs_results.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → When disconnecting: radio option that keeps the connection's query tabs open with their results still shown.
keep_tabs_results.value: Mantener las pestañas y los resultados

leading.location: Settings → Editor → General → Automagic commas → Comma placement: radio option that puts the inserted comma at the start of the new line, before the next item.

none_start_empty_query.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → Restore tabs at launch: radio option that reopens no tabs and starts SQLLY with a single empty query tab.

pinned_tabs_only.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → Restore tabs at launch: radio option that reopens only pinned query tabs when SQLLY starts.

spaces.location: Settings → Editor → General → Indentation: radio option meaning indent with space characters instead of tab characters; pairs with the Tabs option above it.

tabs.location: Settings → Editor → General → Indentation: radio option meaning indent with tab characters; the noun “tabs” here is the tab character, not editor tabs.

trailing.location: Settings → Editor → General → Automagic commas → Comma placement: radio option that puts the inserted comma at the end of the previous line.

accept_table_view.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → When you accept a table or view: section heading (a sentence fragment) above the options for what happens when a table or view completion is accepted.
accept_table_view.value: Cuando aceptas una tabla o vista

alias_names.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Alias names: section heading above the radio options choosing how table aliases are generated when a table is completed.

automagic_commas.location: Settings → Editor → General → Automagic commas: section heading for options that automatically insert missing commas and AND connectors when a list item continues on a new line; “automagic” is a playful word for automatic.

binary_path.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: section heading above the text field holding the full path to the chosen editor's executable program.

bold_text.location: Settings → Editor → General → Bold text: section heading above the checkboxes that choose which kinds of SQL words the editor draws in bold.

date_time_convenience.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense → Date & time convenience: section heading above the options for typing dates in plain words (today, last week, ytd) and turning them into SQL date values.

default_editor.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: section heading above the dropdown listing the supported external editors to choose from.

disconnecting.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs → When disconnecting: section heading (sentence fragment) above the options for what happens to a connection's query tabs when it is disconnected.

display.location: Settings → Editor → General → Display: section heading above the checkboxes that control what the query editor draws (line numbers, statement frame, hover cards, hints, AI summary bar, Vim mode).

feedback_report_object_kinds.location: Settings → Editor → General → Feedback report object kinds: section heading above checkboxes choosing which database object kinds the Improve IntelliSense dialog lists by default.
feedback_report_object_kinds.value: Tipos de objetos del informe de comentarios

indentation.location: Settings → Editor → General → Indentation: section heading above the Tabs / Spaces choice and the spaces-per-tab stepper that control what the Tab key inserts.

intellisense.location: Settings → Editor → General: section heading above the IntelliSense Source dropdown and the IntelliSense feedback report options, near the bottom of the General pane.

matching.location: Settings → Editor → IntelliSense: section heading above the checkboxes that control how typed text is matched against completion suggestions (camel-hump initials, schema-name search).

name.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: section heading above the text input for the display name of a custom editor; shown only when “Other” is chosen in the Default editor dropdown.

navigation.location: Settings → Editor → General: section heading above the camel-hump word movement checkbox, grouping options for how keyboard word-jumps move the caret.

restore_tabs_at_launch.location: Settings → Editor → Tabs: section heading above the radio buttons choosing which query tabs reopen when the app starts (all, pinned only, or none).

selection.location: Settings → Editor → General: section heading above the checkbox that softly highlights other occurrences of the selected word or phrase in the editor.

query_parameters.location: Settings → Editor → General: section heading above the checkbox that turns :name, ? and $1 placeholders written in a query into rows of the Parameters strip.

spacing.location: Settings → Editor → General: section heading above the Auto spacing checkbox, which inserts spaces around SQL operators and punctuation as you type.

invalid_file.location: Settings → Editor → Snippets & Quick Actions → Import from VS Code: error shown under the import buttons when the chosen VS Code / Azure Data Studio snippet file is not valid JSON; {error} is the parser's explanation.
invalid_file.value: No es un archivo de fragmentos de VS Code válido: {error}

not_an_object.location: Settings → Editor → Snippets & Quick Actions → Import from VS Code: error shown under the import buttons when the chosen file is JSON but not a VS Code snippet file (its top level is not an object of named snippets).
not_an_object.value: No es un archivo de fragmentos de VS Code: se esperaba un objeto con fragmentos con nombre.

final_stop_has_default.location: Settings → Editor → Snippets & Quick Actions → Snippet body: validation error shown under the body field and on Save when the final cursor stop $0 is given default text; $0 must stay a plain marker.
final_stop_has_default.value: $0 no puede tener un valor predeterminado

unsupported_syntax.location: Settings → Editor → Snippets & Quick Actions → Snippet body: validation error when the body uses snippet syntax SQLLY does not support; {kind} is an untranslated English word: variable, choice, transform or nested.

unterminated_placeholder.location: Settings → Editor → Snippets & Quick Actions → Snippet body: validation error when a ${…} placeholder in the body is never closed with a brace; {byte} is the character offset where it starts.
unterminated_placeholder.value: Marcador de posición sin cerrar en el byte {byte}

app_store_edition_notice.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: notice box at the top of the pane in the Mac App Store edition only, saying terminal and command-line editors cannot be launched; a “see Help” sentence follows it.
app_store_edition_notice.value: En la edición de Mac App Store solo se abren editores que sean aplicaciones de Mac; no se pueden iniciar editores de línea de comandos ni de terminal.

camel_hump_hint_ctrl.location: Settings → Editor → General → Navigation: help paragraph under the camel-hump word movement checkbox on Windows and Linux, explaining where Ctrl+Left/Right stop inside and between words.
camel_hump_hint_ctrl.value: Ctrl+Izquierda / Ctrl+Derecha (añade Shift para seleccionar) se detienen en cada mayúscula dentro de una palabra y al principio y al final de cada palabra, en lugar de saltar el espacio hasta la siguiente. Ejemplo: en SalesOrderLineId, el cursor se detiene en Sales | Order | Line | Id y después de Id antes de continuar. Los espacios se omiten; una secuencia de puntuación cuenta como una parada.

camel_hump_hint_option.location: Settings → Editor → General → Navigation: help paragraph under the camel-hump word movement checkbox on macOS, explaining where Option+Left/Right stop inside and between words.
camel_hump_hint_option.value: Option+Izquierda / Option+Derecha (añade Shift para seleccionar) se detienen en cada mayúscula dentro de una palabra y al principio y al final de cada palabra, en lugar de saltar el espacio hasta la siguiente. Ejemplo: en SalesOrderLineId, el cursor se detiene en Sales | Order | Line | Id y después de Id antes de continuar. Los espacios se omiten; una secuencia de puntuación cuenta como una parada.

external_editor_path_missing.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: warning under the Binary path field, shown when no executable path is set for the selected editor; prompts the user to fill it in.
external_editor_path_missing.value: Introduce la ruta del ejecutable del editor.

path_not_found.location: Settings → Editor → External Editors: warning under the Binary path field, shown when the entered executable path does not exist on disk, so opening files in that editor will fail.
path_not_found.value: No existe ningún archivo en esta ruta. Abrir con este editor fallará hasta corregirla.

two_finger_result_scroll.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Results: checkbox that turns on two-finger trackpad scrolling to switch between tabbed result sets with left/right swipes.
two_finger_result_scroll.value: Habilitar desplazamiento con dos dedos en los resultados

gestures.location: Settings → Results → Gestures: page title at the top of the Gestures pane, which configures trackpad and modifier-key scrolling.

query_swap_hint.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Query: help paragraph under the 2 finger query swap dropdown, explaining how swiping over the editor opens the query switcher and moves between open queries.
query_swap_hint.value: Cuando está habilitado, deslizar dos dedos sobre el editor de consultas abre el selector de consultas y recorre las consultas abiertas. Ambas direcciones del eje elegido están activas: Arriba / Abajo avanza y retrocede con gestos verticales; Izquierda / Derecha lo hace con gestos horizontales. Si está deshabilitado, el desplazamiento del editor no cambia.

stacked_scroll_hint.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Results: help paragraph under the scroll modifier dropdown, explaining scrolling inside a grid versus the whole stacked results area and tab switching.
stacked_scroll_hint.value: En resultados apilados, desplazarte sobre una cuadrícula desplaza ese conjunto de resultados. Mantén el modificador seleccionado para desplazar toda la pila; al continuar más allá del principio o del final de una cuadrícula, saltas al resultado adyacente. Con el desplazamiento de resultados con dos dedos habilitado, los resultados por pestañas cambian de pestaña al desplazarte a izquierda o derecha; las cuadrículas apiladas siguen desplazándose individualmente.

pane_intro.location: Settings → Results → Gestures: introductory sentence under the pane title summarizing that the pane controls trackpad and modifier-scroll behavior.
pane_intro.value: Configura el comportamiento del trackpad y del desplazamiento con modificadores para los conjuntos de resultados y el cambio de consultas.

multi_result_scroll_modifier.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Results: label of the dropdown choosing which modifier key (None, Shift, Command, Control…) makes scrolling move the whole stack of results instead of one grid.
multi_result_scroll_modifier.value: Modificador de desplazamiento del contenedor de resultados

two_finger_query_swap.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Query: label of the dropdown (Disabled / Vertical / Horizontal) choosing the swipe axis for switching between open query tabs; keep it short.
two_finger_query_swap.value: Cambio de consulta con dos dedos

none.location: Settings → Results → Gestures: modifier summary shown when no modifier keys are selected.
Settings → Results → Gestures → Results: first option in the multi-result scroll modifier dropdown meaning no modifier key is required; other options are key names such as Shift.

query.location: Settings → Results → Gestures: section heading above the 2 finger query swap dropdown, grouping gestures that act on query editor tabs (noun, as in the query editor).

results.location: Settings → Results → Gestures: section heading above the two-finger result-set scrolling checkbox and scroll modifier dropdown, grouping gestures that act on result grids.

limit_scroll_repaints.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Scrolling: checkbox that paces results-grid repaints while scrolling to 60 per second.
limit_scroll_repaints.value: Limitar los repintados durante el desplazamiento a 60 por segundo

detailed_query_timing.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Timing: checkbox that adds the detailed per-query timing breakdown to the results status bar.
detailed_query_timing.value: Mostrar estadísticas detalladas de tiempo por consulta

enable_query_version_history.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Version History: checkbox that turns on per-tab version history, which saves snapshots of the editor text you can later restore.
enable_query_version_history.value: Habilitar el historial de versiones de consultas

git_local_history.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Git: checkbox that lists recent git commits for a tab’s file in the History panel when that file is inside a git repository.
git_local_history.value: Mostrar el historial local de Git en las pestañas vinculadas a un archivo

library_connection_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → SQL Library: checkbox that shows each library file’s remembered connection name beside it in the Library panel.
library_connection_hint.value: Mostrar sugerencia de conexión en archivos de biblioteca

persist_last_results.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: checkbox (desktop only) that saves each tab’s last result grid to disk so it reappears after the app restarts.
persist_last_results.value: Mantener los resultados de cada pestaña entre reinicios

store_query_results_versions.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: checkbox that saves the query results alongside each sealed version, so restoring a version also shows its results.
store_query_results_versions.value: Almacenar resultados de consulta con versiones

performance.location: Settings → Results → Performance: page title at the top of the Performance pane, which tunes query timing display and large result-set memory and paging.
performance.value: Rendimiento

query_history.location: Settings → Editor → Query History: page title at the top of the Query History pane covering version history, execution history, result caching, git history and the SQL Library.

git_history_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Git: help text under the git local history checkbox, describing the read-only commit list shown in the History panel for files in a git work tree.
git_history_hint.value: Lista de solo lectura de commits recientes que modifican el archivo, mostrada en el panel Historial cuando el archivo de la pestaña está dentro de un repositorio de Git.

idle_rollback_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Manual Commit Mode: help text under the idle rollback seconds field, giving the minimum and what happens to an open transaction if the app is killed.
idle_rollback_hint.value: Se aplica a pestañas en modo de confirmación manual. 0 no está permitido; el mínimo es 30. Si la aplicación se cierra forzosamente, el servidor conserva la transacción hasta su propio tiempo de espera por inactividad.

idle_seal_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Version History: help text under the Idle seal interval field, explaining that a pause in typing of that many seconds saves a version.
idle_seal_hint.value: Si dejas de editar durante este número de segundos, el texto del editor se sella como una versión. Mínimo 1.

library_folder_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → SQL Library: help text under the Library folder field explaining folder mapping and the optional first-line comment that remembers a connection; keep the code sample unchanged.
library_folder_hint.value: Las subcarpetas se convierten en carpetas del panel Biblioteca. Los archivos son .sql sin formato; una primera línea opcional `-- sqlly: connection="Name" database=db` recuerda la conexión de destino.

lifecycle_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Lifecycle: help text explaining that closing an unsaved untitled tab discards its version history, while tabs backed by files keep it.
lifecycle_hint.value: Cerrar una pestaña sin título elimina todo su historial. Las pestañas vinculadas a un archivo conservan su historial entre sesiones.

max_versions_eviction.location: Settings → Editor → Query History: help text under the Maximum versions per tab field (listed after the Manual Commit Mode rollback setting), saying the oldest saved versions are deleted once a tab exceeds that number.
max_versions_eviction.value: Las versiones más antiguas se eliminan al superar este número.

memory_budget_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: help text under the Result memory budget field, explaining the per-result-set memory cap, its range, and when it applies.
memory_budget_hint.value: Límite aproximado en MiB para los datos de vista previa mantenidos en memoria por conjunto de resultados. El umbral de filas para volcado a disco limita las filas de vista previa; este presupuesto se alcanza antes con filas anchas. De 1 a 2048 MiB. Se aplica en la próxima consulta.

no_cached_models.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache → Cached data models: empty-state message shown in place of the cache list when no database schemas have been cached yet.
no_cached_models.value: Aún no hay bases de datos en caché. SQLLY crea la caché automáticamente la primera vez que exploras el esquema de una base de datos.

page_chunk_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: help text under the Page chunk size field, explaining how many rows load per page and that as many are released.
page_chunk_hint.value: Filas cargadas por página mientras te desplazas; el mismo número se libera por el lado opuesto para mantener estable el uso de memoria.

page_margin_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: help text under the Page-in margin field, explaining how close to the loaded edge scrolling must get before the next chunk loads.
page_margin_hint.value: Al desplazarte a este número de filas del borde cargado, se carga el siguiente bloque.

resident_rows.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: help text under the Resident rows around view field, describing the rows kept in memory above and below the visible ones.
resident_rows.value: Filas que se mantienen en memoria antes y después de las filas visibles.

result_cache_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: help text under the keep last results checkbox, saying reopened tabs show cached results under a banner until rerun.
result_cache_hint.value: Las pestañas restauradas muestran sus resultados en caché bajo un aviso hasta que vuelvas a ejecutar la consulta. Los resultados más grandes no se almacenan en caché.

retention_cleanup_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Execution History Browser: help text under the retention fields, saying old executions are pruned when Query History opens and pinned statements are kept.
retention_cleanup_hint.value: La limpieza se ejecuta al abrir el Historial de consultas. Las instrucciones fijadas se almacenan por separado y la retención nunca las elimina.

spill_threshold_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: help text under the Spill row threshold field, explaining that bigger result sets are read from a disk file.
spill_threshold_hint.value: Los conjuntos de resultados con más filas que este límite se sirven desde un archivo de volcado en disco en lugar de mantenerse en memoria. Se aplica en la próxima consulta.

storage_eviction_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: help text under the maximum results storage per tab field, saying stored results are dropped before version SQL text when over the limit.
storage_eviction_hint.value: Al superar el límite, los datos de resultados se descartan antes que las entradas SQL.

stored_results_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: help text under the store results with versions checkbox, explaining that restoring a version shows its saved results read-only.
stored_results_hint.value: Restaurar una versión también vuelve a representar sus resultados almacenados, en modo de solo lectura y bajo un aviso informativo. Los resultados se codifican en binario y se comprimen con gzip.

limit_scroll_repaints_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Scrolling: help text under the 60-per-second repaint checkbox explaining the CPU saving on 120 Hz displays and the smoothness trade-off.
limit_scroll_repaints_hint.value: En pantallas de 120 Hz reduce aproximadamente a la mitad la CPU que consume el desplazamiento, con una ligera pérdida de fluidez. El desplazamiento siempre termina en la posición más reciente. Sin efecto en pantallas de 60 Hz.

timing_breakdown_hint.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Timing: help text under the detailed timing checkbox, listing the timing columns shown in the results status bar; First, Query, Server, Paint, Wall and Latency are labels.
timing_breakdown_hint.value: Muestra el desglose Primera respuesta / Consulta / Servidor / Renderizado / Total / Latencia de cada consulta, con los controles para restar latencia y usar hh:MM:ss, en la barra de estado de resultados. Desactivado de forma predeterminada; los recuentos de filas siempre se muestran.

version_size_limit_hint.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: help text under the maximum results per version field, saying results above that size are skipped and the version keeps only its SQL.
version_size_limit_hint.value: Los conjuntos de resultados más grandes no se almacenan; la versión solo conserva su SQL.

execution_retention_days.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Execution History Browser: label of the number field giving how many days executions are kept; 0 means keep them forever.
execution_retention_days.value: Días de retención de ejecuciones (0 = sin límite)

idle_rollback_seconds.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Manual Commit Mode: label of the number field setting how many idle seconds pass before an uncommitted manual-mode transaction is rolled back.
idle_rollback_seconds.value: Revertir transacciones manuales inactivas después de (segundos)

idle_seal_interval_seconds.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Version History: label of the number field setting how many idle seconds after typing stops before the editor text is saved as a version.

library_folder.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → SQL Library: label of the text field holding the disk folder whose .sql files appear in the Library panel; a Choose… button sits beside it.

max_cached_tab_mib.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: label of the number field limiting, in mebibytes, how large a tab’s cached last result may be on disk.
max_cached_tab_mib.value: Tamaño máximo de caché por pestaña (MiB)

max_tab_results_mib.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: label of the number field capping, in mebibytes, the total stored results across all versions of one tab.
max_tab_results_mib.value: Almacenamiento máximo de resultados por pestaña (MiB)

max_version_results_mib.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Storage: label of the number field giving the largest result, in mebibytes, that is stored with a single version.
max_version_results_mib.value: Tamaño máximo de resultados por versión (MiB)

maximum_cached_rows_per_tab.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: label of the number field limiting how many result rows per tab are saved to disk for restore after restart.
maximum_cached_rows_per_tab.value: Número máximo de filas en caché por pestaña

maximum_execution_entries.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Execution History Browser: label of the number field capping how many past query executions are kept in the execution history.
maximum_execution_entries.value: Número máximo de entradas de ejecución

maximum_versions_per_tab.location: Settings → Editor → Query History: label of the number field, listed after the Manual Commit Mode rollback setting, capping how many saved versions each query tab keeps before the oldest are removed.
maximum_versions_per_tab.value: Número máximo de versiones por pestaña

page_chunk_size.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: label of the number field setting how many rows are loaded from the spill file per page while scrolling.

page_margin.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: label of the number field setting how many rows before the loaded edge scrolling triggers loading the next page.

resident_rows_around_view.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: label of the number field setting how many rows stay in memory before and after the visible grid rows.
resident_rows_around_view.value: Filas residentes alrededor de la vista

result_memory_budget_mib.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: label of the number field setting the approximate memory cap, in mebibytes, for preview data of one result set.

spill_row_threshold.location: Settings → Results → Performance → Query Result Optimizations: label of the number field setting the row count above which a result set is written to a disk spill file.
spill_row_threshold.value: Umbral de filas para volcado a disco

performance_intro.location: Settings → Results → Performance: introductory sentence under the pane title summarizing that it tunes disk spilling and memory paging of large result sets.
performance_intro.value: Ajusta cómo se vuelcan a disco los conjuntos de resultados grandes y cómo se cargan y descargan de la memoria al desplazarte.

schema_cache_intro.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: introductory paragraph at the top of the pane explaining that database schemas are cached on disk, why, and what clearing a cache does.
schema_cache_intro.value: SQLLY almacena en disco el esquema de cada base de datos para que IntelliSense y el Explorador de servidores estén listos al reconectar, sin esperar una nueva descarga de metadatos. Borra una caché para recuperar espacio; SQLLY la reconstruirá desde el servidor la próxima vez que abras esa base de datos.

version_history_intro.location: Settings → Editor → Query History: introductory paragraph under the pane title explaining what per-tab version history is, when versions are saved, and where to restore them.
version_history_intro.value: Historial de versiones por pestaña para los editores de consultas. Una versión se sella al ejecutar la consulta o al pausar la edición; restaura cualquier versión desde el panel Historial sin perder el texto actual.

click_again_clear.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: label of the Clear all button after its first click, asking for a second click to confirm; {value} is a counted phrase such as “3 caches”.
click_again_clear.value: Haz clic de nuevo para borrar {value}

choose.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → SQL Library: small button beside the Library folder field that opens a folder picker to choose the library folder.

clear.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache → Cached data models: small button at the right of each cached database row that deletes that one cached schema.

clear_result_cache.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: small button that deletes every tab’s cached last result from disk; the first click only arms it.

clear_result_cache_confirm.location: Settings → Editor → Query History → Result Cache: label of the clear cached results button after its first click, asking for a second click to confirm the deletion.
clear_result_cache_confirm.value: Haz clic de nuevo para borrar los resultados en caché

cached_data_models.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: section heading above the list of cached database schemas, grouped by server with each database’s size and age.

default_default.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → App Commands list: dim caption under each app command's binding cells showing its built-in shortcut; {default} is the default key combination (or combinations) for the current profile.

default_default_display.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Editor Actions list: dim caption on each SQL editor action row showing its built-in shortcut; {default_display} is the platform's default key combination for that editor action.

editor_action_conflict.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Editor Actions list: warning shown when the key combination just pressed while rebinding a SQL editor action already belongs to another editor action; {stroke} is the combination, {titles} the clashing action names joined with “and”.
editor_action_conflict.value: {stroke} ya está asignado a {titles}. Elige otro atajo.

save_app_shortcuts_failed.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → App Commands → Save: error shown when application shortcut overrides cannot be saved.
save_app_shortcuts_failed.value: No se pudieron guardar los atajos: {error}

save_editor_shortcuts_failed.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Editor Actions → Save: error shown when editor shortcut overrides cannot be saved.
save_editor_shortcuts_failed.value: No se pudieron guardar los atajos: {error}

search_hint.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Search: hint under the search box giving how many rows match the filter and how to rebind; {visible} and {total_count} count app commands, {editor_visible} editor actions. The two file paths are literal and must stay unchanged.
search_hint.value: Mostrando {visible} de {total_count} comandos de aplicación y {editor_visible} acciones del editor. Haz clic en cualquier atajo para reasignarlo. Presiona Esc para cancelar. Personalizaciones de la aplicación: ~/Library/Application Support/SQLLY/keybindings.json. Personalizaciones del editor: ~/Library/Application Support/SQLLY/editor-keybindings.json

custom.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Profile: label of the profile button (also shown in the pane intro) for a user-defined shortcut set that starts from the defaults and keeps the user's own overrides.

macos_native.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Profile: label of the default profile button on macOS (also shown in the pane intro), selecting the standard Mac-style shortcut set; “macOS” is a product name.

platform_native.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Profile: label of the default profile button on Windows and Linux (also in the pane intro), selecting the shortcut set native to the user's operating system.

reset.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → App Commands list: small button at the end of an app command row, shown only when that command has a custom shortcut; restores the command's default binding (verb).

reset_2.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts → Editor Actions list: small button at the end of a SQL editor action row, shown only when that action has a custom shortcut; removes the override and restores the default (verb).

button.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: button at the bottom of the pane, below both shortcut lists, that starts resetting every app and editor shortcut override; first click only arms it and asks for a second click.

confirm_button.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: replacement text of the bottom “Reset All Overrides” button after the first click, asking for a second click to confirm discarding every custom shortcut.
confirm_button.value: Haz clic de nuevo para restablecer todas las personalizaciones

app_commands.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: section heading above the scrollable list of application-wide commands (menus, tabs, windows) and their rebindable shortcuts, below the search hint.

editor_actions.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: section heading above the scrollable list of SQL query editor actions (cursor movement, selection, editing) and their rebindable shortcuts, below the app commands list.

profile.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: section heading above the row of shortcut profile buttons (native, SSMS, Custom) near the top of the pane; noun meaning a preset set of shortcuts.

search.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: section heading above the search box that filters both shortcut lists by command name or key; noun.

reset_all_warning.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: warning shown under the bottom reset button after its first click, while it waits for the confirming second click, explaining that all custom shortcuts will be lost permanently.
reset_all_warning.value: Esto descarta todos los atajos personalizados de la aplicación y del editor. No se puede deshacer.

restart_required.location: Settings → Workspace → Keyboard Shortcuts: warning shown near the top of the pane after a shortcut is changed, telling the user the change is saved but some places only pick it up after restarting the app.
restart_required.value: Los cambios de atajos se han guardado. Reinicia SQLLY para activarlos en todas partes.

feature_unavailable.location: Settings → AI → MCP Servers (browser build): clause naming MCP server management as unavailable, inserted as {feature} into the browser-preview notice shown instead of the MCP settings pane.
feature_unavailable.value: La gestión de servidores MCP no está disponible

file_export_options.location: Settings → Results → Export: section heading partway down the Export pane, separating the general export settings above from the file-format options below (NULL text, line breaks) used when saving grid results to files.

settings.location: Settings → Dialog: title shown in the unified dialog title bar.

arguments.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: label above the Arguments input, shown only for the stdio transport; space-separated command-line arguments passed to the server program.

command.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: label above the Command input, shown only for the stdio transport; the program SQLLY launches to run a local MCP server.

environment.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: label above the multi-line Environment box (stdio only); explains the KEY=VALUE-per-line format and that values are kept in the system Keychain, not the servers JSON file.
environment.value: Entorno (KEY=VALUE por línea: se almacena en el llavero, no en el archivo JSON)

name.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: label above the Name input, shown for both transports; the display name of the external MCP server, which must be unique.

url.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: label above the URL input, shown only when the HTTP transport is selected; the endpoint address of a remote MCP server.

ai_tool_digest.location: AI panel → Conversation system prompt (not shown on screen): instruction sent to the AI model listing tools of enabled external MCP servers and saying they may only be mentioned or recommended; {value} is the semicolon-separated per-server list.
ai_tool_digest.value: Herramientas externas disponibles a través de servidores MCP (SQLLY no las ejecuta; solo puedes mencionarlas o recomendarlas al usuario): {value}

could_not_reach_server_error.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the Test request to an HTTP MCP server cannot be sent (network, DNS, TLS); {error} is the technical reason.
could_not_reach_server_error.value: No se pudo contactar con el servidor: {error}

could_not_start_server_error.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the stdio server's Command cannot be launched during Test (e.g. program not found); {error} is the OS reason.
could_not_start_server_error.value: No se pudo iniciar el servidor: {error}

could_not_write_server_error.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → stdio test: error shown when a request cannot be written to the server.
could_not_write_server_error.value: No se pudo escribir en el servidor: {error}

count_tools.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: success text after “✓” when the server lists more tools than SQLLY keeps; {identity} is the server name/version line, {count} kept tools, {total_tools} the server's total.

count_tools_2.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: success text after “✓” when all the server's tools were captured; {identity} is the server name/version line, {count} is the number of tools discovered.

env_keychain_save_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: error shown when Add Server/Update Server cannot store the environment variables in the system Keychain; {error} is the reason.
env_keychain_save_failed.value: No se pudo guardar el entorno en el llavero: {error}

handshake_timeout.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the server does not complete the Test handshake before the time limit; {value} is the number of seconds waited.
handshake_timeout.value: El servidor no respondió en {value} segundos

http_client_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the HTTP client for testing an HTTP server cannot be set up; {error} is the technical reason.
http_client_failed.value: No se pudo crear el cliente HTTP: {error}

http_read_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → HTTP test: error shown when the server response cannot be read.
http_read_failed.value: No se pudo leer la respuesta del servidor: {error}

initialize_rejected.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the server answers the initialize request with an error; {message} is the server's own error message.

last_seen.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row → Tool summary line: suffix appended after the tool count when the list comes from an earlier Test rather than this session; {value} is a date and time or “at an earlier test”.

more.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers: suffix appended to a server's visible tool list when additional tools remain on the server; includes the leading separator space.

more_2.location: AI panel → Conversation system prompt (not shown on screen): one server's entry in the external MCP tool digest; {name} is the server name, {value_2} its comma-separated tools, {more} an optional “more on the server” note.

more_server.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row → Tool summary line: note appended after the tool count when the server offered more tools than SQLLY stores; {tools_truncated} is the number left out.

production_always_refused.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Connections list: checkbox label for a saved connection marked as production, shown greyed and disabled; {name} is the connection name, noting MCP clients can never use it.

server_answered_status_brief.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when an HTTP MCP server replies with an error status; {status} is the HTTP status code and text, {brief} the start of the response body.

server_info.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: server identity shown after “✓” on a successful Test, built from the server's initialize reply; {name} is the server's own name, {version} its version, {protocol} the MCP protocol version.

server_named_already_exists.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: validation error shown when Add Server/Update Server would create a second server with the same name (case-insensitive); {name} is the entered name.
server_named_already_exists.value: Ya existe un servidor con el nombre {name}

stdio_flush_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → HTTP test: error shown when a request cannot be written to the server.
stdio_flush_failed.value: No se pudo escribir en el servidor: {error}

stdio_read_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → stdio test: error shown when the server response cannot be read.
stdio_read_failed.value: No se pudo leer la respuesta del servidor: {error}

tools_list_rejected.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: error produced when the server answers the tool-list request with an error; {message} is the server's message. Tool discovery is best-effort, so the Test still succeeds and this rarely appears.

add_server.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: button below the form fields that saves the entered values as a new external MCP server; replaced by Update Server while editing.

allow_private_network_label.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers: checkbox label above the server list; when ticked, Test may contact HTTPS servers at link-local or cloud-metadata addresses, which are blocked by default for safety.
allow_private_network_label.value: Permitir que la prueba HTTP acceda a hosts de enlace local y de metadatos de la nube (desactivado de forma predeterminada).

answer_has_no_json.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when an HTTP server's response to initialize contains no JSON message at all.
answer_has_no_json.value: La respuesta del servidor no contenía JSON

ceiling_read_write_confirm.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Global ceiling: second selectable choice beside “Read-only (default)”; MCP clients may propose writes, which open in SQLLY for the user to confirm.
ceiling_read_write_confirm.value: Lectura/escritura con confirmación: las escrituras se abren en SQLLY para que las confirmes

command_required_stdio_server.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: validation error shown when saving a stdio server whose Command field is empty.
command_required_stdio_server.value: El comando es obligatorio para un servidor stdio

copied_claude_code_snippet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: confirmation in the status line after clicking Copy for Claude Code; the Claude Code setup command for sqlly-cli is now on the clipboard.
copied_claude_code_snippet.value: Se copió el fragmento de instalación de Claude Code.

copied_claude_desktop_snippet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: confirmation in the status line after clicking Copy for Claude Desktop; the Claude Desktop configuration snippet for sqlly-cli is now on the clipboard.
copied_claude_desktop_snippet.value: Se copió el fragmento de instalación de Claude Desktop.

copied_cursor_install_snippet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: confirmation in the status line after clicking Copy for Cursor; the Cursor configuration snippet for sqlly-cli is now on the clipboard.
copied_cursor_install_snippet.value: Se copió el fragmento de instalación de Cursor.

copied_vs_code_snippet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: confirmation in the status line after clicking Copy for VS Code; the VS Code configuration snippet for sqlly-cli is now on the clipboard.
copied_vs_code_snippet.value: Se copió el fragmento de instalación de VS Code.

copied_windsurf_snippet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: confirmation in the status line after clicking Copy for Windsurf; the Windsurf configuration snippet for sqlly-cli is now on the clipboard.
copied_windsurf_snippet.value: Se copió el fragmento de instalación de Windsurf.

could_not_open_server_s_input.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the launched stdio server's standard input pipe cannot be opened, so SQLLY cannot send it requests.
could_not_open_server_s_input.value: No se pudo abrir la entrada del servidor

env_format_invalid.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: validation error shown when saving a stdio server whose Environment box contains an entry not in KEY=VALUE form.
env_format_invalid.value: El entorno debe contener pares KEY=VALUE, uno por línea o separados por ;

exited_before_initialize.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the launched stdio server program quits before replying to the initialize request.
exited_before_initialize.value: El servidor se cerró antes de responder a la inicialización

external_servers_intro.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers: introductory paragraph above the external server list explaining what these servers are and that Test performs a real handshake and lists tools for the AI to mention.
external_servers_intro.value: Servidores de Model Context Protocol con los que SQLLY puede comunicarse. La prueba realiza un protocolo de enlace initialize real y enumera las herramientas del servidor para que la IA pueda mencionarlas; la ejecución de herramientas por la IA es un paso posterior.

handshake_task_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the background Test job itself crashes or is cancelled before producing a result.
handshake_task_failed.value: Error en la tarea de protocolo de enlace

http_test_url_refused.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when Test is refused because an HTTP server's URL is not https:// or plain http:// to the local machine.
http_test_url_refused.value: La prueba HTTP solo permite https:// o http:// a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1

inherit_global.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Connections list: label of the per-connection mode button meaning the connection follows the global ceiling; clicking cycles to Locked, Read-only, Read/write with confirm.

initialize_no_answer.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when a stdio server prints many lines but none is a reply to the initialize request.
initialize_no_answer.value: El servidor nunca respondió a la solicitud initialize

locked.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Connections list: label of the per-connection mode button meaning MCP clients may not use this connection at all; clicking cycles to the next mode.

name_required.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: validation error shown when Add Server/Update Server is clicked with an empty Name field.

not_available.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Test: status shown when server testing is unavailable.

not_available_2.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Tool execution: status shown when tool execution is unavailable.

open_stdout_failed.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the launched stdio server's standard output pipe cannot be opened, so SQLLY cannot read its replies.
open_stdout_failed.value: No se pudo abrir la salida del servidor

policy_saved.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server: confirmation in the status line under the install buttons after any policy change (global ceiling, connections, mode, limits) is saved.

read_only.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Connections list: label of the per-connection mode button meaning MCP clients may only read from this connection; clicking cycles to the next mode.

read_only_default.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Global ceiling: first of two selectable choices; MCP clients may only read data. It is the default.

read_write_confirm.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Connections list: short label of the per-connection mode button allowing writes that the user must confirm in SQLLY; clicking cycles back to Inherit global.

server_added.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: confirmation shown after Add Server saves a new external MCP server.

server_did_not_answer_json.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the server's reply to the initialize request is not valid JSON.
server_did_not_answer_json.value: El servidor no respondió con JSON

server_intro.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server: introductory paragraph under the section title explaining that external AI tools can use saved connections read-only, production is refused, and how each database enforces read-only.
server_intro.value: Permite que Claude Code, Cursor y otros clientes MCP usen tus conexiones guardadas en modo de solo lectura. Los secretos permanecen en el llavero del sistema. Las conexiones de producción siempre se rechazan. La base de datos aplica el modo de solo lectura, no solo la comprobación SQL de SQLLY: cada consulta se ejecuta en una transacción de solo lectura que siempre se revierte (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB), en modo de solo consulta en SQLite y, en SQL Server —que no tiene transacciones de solo lectura—, dentro de una transacción revertida más un filtro de instrucciones.

server_s_answer_has_no_result.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: failure text after “✗” when the server's initialize reply is JSON but lacks the expected result section.
server_s_answer_has_no_result.value: La respuesta del servidor no incluye ningún resultado

server_test_unavailable.location: Browser-hosted SQLLY → Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers: feature name inserted into the not-available-in-browser message when Test is clicked; noun phrase naming the action.
server_test_unavailable.value: La prueba de servidores MCP no está disponible

server_updated.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: confirmation shown after Update Server saves changes to an existing external MCP server.

start_stdio_server.location: Mac App Store edition → Settings → AI → MCP → Server row test result: feature name inserted into the sandbox-limitation message when Test is clicked for a stdio server; a noun phrase naming the action.

testing.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: lowercase progress text under the row while its Test is running; the Test button is disabled until it finishes.

tools_array_missing.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: error produced when the tool-list reply lacks a tools list; tool discovery is best-effort, so the Test still succeeds and this rarely appears.
tools_array_missing.value: La respuesta de tools/list no contiene una matriz de herramientas

tools_list_not_json.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row test result: error produced when the reply to the tool-list request is not valid JSON; tool discovery is best-effort, so the Test still succeeds and this rarely appears.
tools_list_not_json.value: El servidor no respondió a tools/list con JSON

update_server.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: button below the form fields, shown instead of Add Server while editing an existing server; saves the changes to that server.

url_scheme_error.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Status line below the form: validation error shown when saving an HTTP server whose URL is not https://, or plain http:// to the local machine.
url_scheme_error.value: La URL debe ser https://, o http:// solo para localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1

plural.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: clickable tool summary under a tested server with two or more tools; {icon} is a ▸/▾ expand arrow, {tool_count} the number of tools. Plural form.

single.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: clickable tool summary under a tested server with exactly one tool; {icon} is a ▸/▾ expand arrow, {tool_count} is 1. Singular form.

all_connections.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Connections: All connections policy-scope option.

ceiling_note.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server: note below the Global ceiling choices explaining per-connection modes can only restrict further, and that rate limits reset when the MCP server restarts.
ceiling_note.value: Los modos por conexión solo pueden ser más estrictos que el límite global. Los límites de frecuencia se restablecen cuando se reinicia el servidor MCP.

connections.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Connections: section heading for per-connection policies.

global_ceiling.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Policy: Global ceiling section heading.

idle_timeout_s.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: Idle timeout input label in seconds.

install.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Installation: Install section heading.

install_command_hint.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: hint below the sqlly-cli path input giving the terminal command that builds and installs sqlly-cli from source; keep the command itself unchanged.

limits.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: section heading for request and output limits.

max_chars_per_cell_2000.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: maximum characters per cell input label.

max_ddl_per_minute_20.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: maximum DDL statements per minute input label.

max_queries_per_minute_600.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: maximum queries per minute input label.

max_rows_100.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: maximum returned rows input label.

max_writes_per_minute_60.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Limits: maximum writes per minute input label.

no_mcp_servers_configured_yet.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server list: empty state shown before any external MCP server is configured.
no_mcp_servers_configured_yet.value: Aún no hay servidores MCP configurados.

sqlly_as_mcp_server.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server: pane heading for the local MCP server integration.

sqlly_as_mcp_server_2.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Installation: heading for installing the local MCP server integration.

sqlly_cli_path.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as MCP server → Installation: sqlly-cli executable path input label.

transport.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add or edit server: transport selector label.

cancel_edit.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Add/edit server form: button beside Update Server, shown only while editing an existing server; discards the edit and returns the form to adding a new server.

copy_claude_code.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: first button in the row under the snippet box; copies the command that registers sqlly-cli as an MCP server in Claude Code.

copy_claude_desktop.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: button in the row under the snippet box; copies the configuration snippet that adds sqlly-cli to Claude Desktop.

copy_cursor.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: button in the row under the snippet box; copies the configuration snippet that adds sqlly-cli to the Cursor editor.

copy_vs_code.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: button in the row under the snippet box; copies the configuration snippet that adds sqlly-cli to VS Code.

copy_windsurf.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: button in the row under the snippet box; copies the configuration snippet that adds sqlly-cli to the Windsurf editor.

edit.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: small button between Test and Remove that loads this server's settings into the form below for editing.

open_mcp_activity.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: last button in the row under the snippet box; opens the MCP Activity window showing what external MCP clients have done.

remove.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: last small button on the row; immediately deletes this external MCP server and its stored environment, with no confirmation.

test.location: Settings → AI → MCP → External MCP servers → Server row: first small button on the row; connects to the server, performs the MCP handshake and lists its tools, showing the result under the row.

sqlly_cli_path.location: Settings → AI → MCP → SQLLY as an MCP server → Install: placeholder in the sqlly-cli path input, shown when empty; the file path to the sqlly-cli program used in the copied install snippets.

align_center.location: Settings → Results → Date, Boolean, Unique ID, Integer and Decimal panes → Alignment: dropdown option that centers values of that type in result grid cells.

align_left.location: Settings → Results → Date, Boolean, Unique ID, Integer and Decimal panes → Alignment: dropdown option that left-aligns values of that type in result grid cells; the default.

align_right.location: Settings → Results → Date, Boolean, Unique ID, Integer and Decimal panes → Alignment: dropdown option that right-aligns values of that type in result grid cells.

always_local.location: Settings → Results → Date → Time zone: dropdown option that converts date-time values to the computer's local time zone before display.

always_utc.location: Settings → Results → Date → Time zone: dropdown option, the default, that shows date-time values converted to UTC.

boolean.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that formats the matched column as true/false values.

built.location: Settings → Editor → General → IntelliSense → Source: dropdown option choosing the built-in local SQL parser for completions (as opposed to the Rust engine).

date.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option, the first and default choice, that formats the matched column as a date/time.

decimal.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that formats the matched column as a decimal number with set places and separators.

disabled.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Query → 2 finger query swap: dropdown option, the default, that turns off the two-finger swipe for switching queries.

epoch_datetime.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that shows a numeric Unix epoch timestamp column as a readable date and time.

horizontal.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Query → 2 finger query swap: dropdown option that switches queries with a left/right two-finger swipe over the editor.

integer.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that formats the matched column as a whole number.

json_path.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that shows only the value at a JSON path (such as $.a.b) extracted from a JSON column.

mask.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that hides the column's value behind mask characters, keeping only a set prefix and suffix visible.

native_as_stored.location: Settings → Results → Date → Time zone: dropdown option that shows date-time values exactly as the database stored them, with no time-zone conversion.

number_style.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that formats the column with a chosen number style (decimals, thousands separators).

rust_engine.location: Settings → Editor → General → IntelliSense → Source: dropdown option choosing the more complete Rust-based SQL parser engine for completions; “Rust” is a product name.

specific_time_zone.location: Settings → Results → Date → Time zone: dropdown option that converts date-time values to one named time zone, revealing a field to choose it.

template.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Add override → Kind: dropdown option that renders the column through a text template such as {value|upper}.

text_inherit.location: Settings → Results → Column overrides → Kind: display name of the plain-text kind, meaning no special formatting is applied and the column keeps the default display.

vertical.location: Settings → Results → Gestures → Query → 2 finger query swap: dropdown option that switches queries with an up/down two-finger swipe over the editor.

just_now.location: Settings → Results → IntelliSense Cache → Cached data models → Last refresh: timestamp shown immediately after a cache refresh.

open_cache_folder.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: button at the left of the actions row (Linux and other platforms) that opens the folder holding cached database schemas in the file manager.

recently_2.location: Settings → Results → IntelliSense Cache → Cached data models → Created: approximate timestamp for a recently created cache.

reveal_in_finder.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: button at the left of the actions row on macOS that shows the folder holding cached database schemas in Finder.

show_in_explorer.location: Settings → IntelliSense Cache: button at the left of the actions row on Windows that shows the folder holding cached database schemas in File Explorer.
show_in_explorer.value: Mostrar en el Explorador de archivos

unknown_server.location: Settings → Results → IntelliSense Cache → Cached data models → Server column: fallback shown when the server name is unavailable.

cloud.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens the cloud AI providers page where hosted provider profiles, endpoints, models and API keys are configured.

coding_agent_cli.location: Settings → Sidebar and breadcrumb: navigation destination reading “Coding agent CLI” at Settings → ai → coding_agent_cli.

decision_model.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens the page for the small fast model that answers quick pick-one, rating or yes/no questions for other features.

fim.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens settings for inline fill-in-the-middle (FIM) autocomplete in the SQL editor powered by a local Ollama model; keep “FIM” as an abbreviation.

mcp.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens the list of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers SQLLY connects to for tool discovery; keep “MCP” untranslated.

on_device.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens settings for AI features that run locally through Ollama on this computer, so SQL never leaves the machine.

playground.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → AI folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens a scratch area for sending a single test prompt to a configured AI model; nothing typed there is saved.

title.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → Top level: folder name in the settings sidebar and first breadcrumb segment; groups all AI pages (On device, Autocomplete, Cloud, Decision model, Coding agent CLI, MCP, Playground).

display.location: Settings → Sidebar tree → Appearance folder: page name in the settings sidebar, also the last breadcrumb segment and the settings-search result label; opens fonts and sizes for the workbench (text size, editor and grid fonts).
